abstract: >-
  Theories of third-language (L3) morphosyntactic transfer disagree over whether prior
  grammars are transferred whole or property by property. The Typological Primacy Model
  predicts that similarity in the lexicon selects the grammar that is transferred, whereas
  property-by-property accounts allow a prior-language property to be recruited whatever the
  lexicon resembles. We trained 65 Norwegian--English bilinguals on Mini-Norwegian or
  Mini-English, miniature languages sharing their grammatical morphemes but built on
  Norwegian or English words, and recorded grammaticality judgements and event-related
  potentials (ERPs) to three properties across four sessions, the last a retention test
  months later. For gender agreement, which Norwegian has and English lacks,
  signal-detection analyses of the judgements showed the Mini-Norwegian group to be no more
  sensitive than the Mini-English group at any session. In the
  ERPs, gender-agreement violations elicited a negativity that grew across sessions in the
  late window; neither it nor its growth differed credibly between groups.
  In the later sessions, Mini-Norwegian learners more readily judged gender-agreement
  sentences grammatical, ungrammatical ones included, a criterion difference not credible
  once each learner's change in criterion was modelled. Differential
  object marking and verb--object number agreement, absent from both prior languages, showed
  no credible group difference in sensitivity at any session. The absence of a Mini-Norwegian advantage is what
  property-by-property accounts allow and lexically cued wholesale transfer does not. Without
  a measurement before training or a comparison group lacking gender, the design
  narrows the debate without settling it. Lexical similarity brought no sensitivity
  advantage, and its influence on acceptance remains suggestive.
keywords: [L3 acquisition, morphosyntactic transfer, ERP, artificial language, signal detection theory, Bayesian multilevel models]
bibliography: references.bib
floatsintext: true
author-note:
  correspondence-note: >

    Department of Education, University of Oxford, 15 Norham Gardens, Oxford OX2 6PY,

format:
  apaquarto-pdf:
    documentmode: man
    pdf-engine: lualatex
    include-in-header:
      - text: |
          % apaquarto's template decrements the table counter at the end of every
          % longtable that carries no caption of its own (apatemplate.tex, "Disable
          % longtable counter"). Quarto now places the caption on an enclosing table
          % float and marks the longtable \def\LTcaptype{none}, so no longtable
          % carries its own caption any more and that decrement cancels the increment
          % the \caption just made. Without this, every table prints as "Table 1" and
          % every cross-reference to a table resolves to 1 -- in the PDF only; the
          % HTML and DOCX outputs number correctly. Restore the lost increment.
          \makeatletter
          \AtBeginDocument{%
            \apptocmd{\endlongtable}{\ifLTpatch@caption\else\addtocounter{table}{1}\fi}{}{}%
          }
          \makeatother

          % --- Vertical rhythm -------------------------------------------------
          % Defaults left captions crowded against their table or figure, opened a
          % gap above and below every display equation that broke the flow of the
          % surrounding sentence, and put more space under a heading than over it,
          % which detaches the heading from the text it introduces.
          % caption.sty is already loaded by the apa7 class, so only its settings are
          % adjusted here; loading it again risks an option clash.
          \captionsetup{aboveskip=10pt, belowskip=10pt}
          % apa7 forces \flushbottom, which stretches the flexible vertical glue
          % between paragraphs when a page happens to end unevenly. In a double-
          % spaced manuscript that can create conspicuous, page-specific gaps in
          % the running text. Keep paragraph spacing stable and let the page bottom
          % remain naturally ragged instead.
          \raggedbottom
          % Keep multi-line displays compact without changing the manuscript's
          % double spacing in ordinary prose.
          \AtBeginDocument{%
            \setlength{\jot}{0pt}%
            \setlength{\abovedisplayskip}{4pt}%
            \setlength{\belowdisplayskip}{4pt}%
            \setlength{\abovedisplayshortskip}{2pt}%
            \setlength{\belowdisplayshortskip}{2pt}%
          }
          % Heading spacing is left to the apa7 class. The titlesec package cannot parse
          % that class's redefined heading levels: it fails at \ttl@extract\subparagraph
          % with 'Argument of \subparagraph has an extra }', and the document does not
          % build with it loaded. The spacing the class applies is APA's own, which is
          % what a journal expects, and the roomy look in manuscript mode comes from the
          % required double spacing rather than from the heading skips.

          % --- Tables ------------------------------------------------------------
          % Pandoc writes every table as a longtable, so these settings reach every
          % table. Every table chunk sets apa-longtable: true, which places the
          % longtable in the running text: nested in a table float instead, a table
          % cannot break across pages, and Table 1's note, the next heading and a
          % paragraph were pushed below the page edge.
          % The body is single-spaced at 10 pt (\footnotesize of the 12 pt
          % class), which APA 7 permits for tables, with 4 pt column padding and a
          % little extra row height (\LESarraystretch; the long convergence tables
          % of Appendix D set it to 1 around their chunks). Nothing here scales a
          % table: the column widths are set by the table code, through
          % _shared/lua/apa-table-heads.lua where they are given exactly.
          % apatemplate.tex redefines \endlongtable to add an \hline under Pandoc's
          % \bottomrule, which printed a double bottom rule, so the original ending
          % is restored. The table-counter fix above is appended at the start of the
          % document and so still applies.
          % etoolbox supplies \AtBeginEnvironment and \apptocmd; needspace supplies
          % \Needspace.
          \usepackage{etoolbox}
          \usepackage{graphicx}
          \usepackage{needspace}
          \newcommand{\LESarraystretch}{1.2}
          \AtBeginEnvironment{longtable}{\renewcommand{\baselinestretch}{1}\footnotesize\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{\LESarraystretch}}
          \makeatletter\def\endlongtable{\endoldlt}\makeatother
          % A table is kept with its note (LOCAL PATCH in apafloatlatex.lua). The
          % patch typesets the caption title and the note into \LEScapbox and
          % \LESnotebox, calls \LESneedtable with the number of head and body rows,
          % and, for a table with a note, wraps it in \LESnoteintable.
          % \LESnoteintable sets the note as the table's last row, below the
          % bottom rule (drawn there in place of Pandoc's rule in the last foot),
          % with no page break allowed above it. longtable's own page breaking
          % then keeps the note with the last rows, carrying them to the next page
          % under the repeated caption and heads when the note does not fit, so a
          % note can never be cut off from its table or land above the next one.
          % The note row is \rlap'ed: it is as wide as the text and does not widen
          % the table's last column.
          % \LESneedtable decides where the table starts. The height needed is the
          % rows at the table's row pitch, the caption, the note and
          % \LEStableextra (the space above the caption, the "Table N" line, the
          % rules and the gap before the note). When that height is within
          % \LESwholetable of the text height, the table is moved to the next page
          % whole if it does not fit on this one. A longer table breaks across
          % pages anyway, so it only needs room for its caption, heads and a first
          % block of rows. The check is made twice: a figure deferred from the
          % page being left is placed at the top of the next one, which the first
          % check cannot see, so after a break an empty rule starts the new page
          % (the space it and the table's \LTpre would add at the top is taken
          % back), and the table moves on once more if it still does not fit.
          % \LESneed is a dimen, not a skip: assigning a skip scans on for "plus"
          % and "minus", which expanded the \ifdim below before the new value was
          % stored.
          \newbox\LEScapbox
          \newbox\LESnotebox
          \newdimen\LESneed
          \newdimen\LEStableextra
          \LEStableextra=1in
          \newcommand{\LESwholetable}{0.75}
          \makeatletter
          % #1: the skip that follows a page-starting rule (\LTpre for a table)
          \newcommand{\LESneedtable}[2][\z@]{%
            \par
            \def\LES@pre{#1}%
            \begingroup
              \renewcommand{\baselinestretch}{1}\footnotesize
              \dimen@=\LESarraystretch\baselineskip
              \global\LESneed=\dimexpr #2\dimen@ + \ht\LEScapbox + \dp\LEScapbox
                + \LEStableextra + \ht\LESnotebox + \dp\LESnotebox\relax
              \ifdim\LESneed>\LESwholetable\textheight
                \global\LESneed=\dimexpr 10\dimen@ + \ht\LEScapbox + \dp\LEScapbox
                  + \LEStableextra\relax
              \fi
            \endgroup
            \LES@needcheck\LES@needcheck}
          \newcommand{\LES@needcheck}{%
            \par\penalty-100
            \begingroup
              \dimen@ii\pagegoal \advance\dimen@ii-\pagetotal
              \ifdim\LESneed>\dimen@ii
                \ifdim\dimen@ii>\z@ \vfil\fi
                \break
                \hrule\@height\z@\@width\z@ \vskip-\topskip \vskip-\LES@pre
              \fi
            \endgroup}
          % \LESnoteintable is used inside a group around the table. The rule is
          % booktabs' own bottom rule, which in a longtable is a row spanning the
          % table's columns with no page break allowed above it. booktabs then
          % adds its below-rule space as breakable glue; for this one rule
          % (\ifLES@lastrule) the space is bracketed by \nobreak instead, and 10 pt
          % more separate the rule from the note, whose box opens with the note's
          % own 8 pt.
          \newif\ifLES@lastrule
          \AtBeginDocument{%
            \let\LES@BTendrule\@BTendrule
            \def\@BTendrule{\ifLES@lastrule
              \expandafter\LES@BTendlast\else\expandafter\LES@BTendrule\fi}}
          \def\LES@BTendlast{\global\LES@lastrulefalse\global\@lastruleclass\z@
            \nobreak\vskip\dimexpr\@belowrulesep+10pt\relax\nobreak\ifnum0=`{\fi}}
          \newcommand{\LESnoteintable}{%
            \let\LES@bottomrule\bottomrule
            \def\bottomrule{}%
            \let\LES@endlongtable\endlongtable
            \def\endlongtable{\LES@noterow\LES@endlongtable}}
          \newcommand{\LES@noterow}{%
            \noalign{\global\LES@lastruletrue}\LES@bottomrule
            \multicolumn{\the\LT@cols}{@{}l@{}}{\rlap{\box\LESnotebox}}\\}
          \makeatother
          % A table's group and subgroup rows are kept with the row below them, and
          % the rows of one block (a window, a contrast block) with each other. The
          % table code ends each such row's first cell with \LESkeepnext (PDF
          % only); the next row end then acts as longtable's \\*, which forbids a
          % page break after the row, so a group heading is never left alone at
          % the foot of a page and a continuation page never opens on rows cut off
          % from their label.
          \newif\ifLESkeepnext
          \newcommand{\LESkeepnext}{\global\LESkeepnexttrue}
          \makeatletter
          \AtBeginDocument{%
            \let\LES@LT@tabularcr\LT@tabularcr
            \protected\def\LT@tabularcr{%
              \ifLESkeepnext\global\LESkeepnextfalse
                \expandafter\@firstoftwo\else\expandafter\@secondoftwo\fi
              {\LES@LT@tabularcr*}{\LES@LT@tabularcr}}%
          }
          \makeatother
          % Centre the content of every float. The notes restore the paragraph
          % shape of running text (LOCAL PATCH in apafloatlatex.lua).
          \makeatletter
          \g@addto@macro\@floatboxreset{\centering}
          \makeatother
    # cairo_pdf embeds the fonts it uses and renders the Unicode minus, micro and
    # multiplication signs the figures contain; R's default pdf() device references
    # Helvetica without embedding it, which submission systems flag.
    knitr:
      opts_chunk:
        dev: "cairo_pdf"
  apaquarto-html: default
  apaquarto-docx:
    fig-dpi: 600
    # ragg renders the same Unicode signs (minus, micro, multiplication, prime, en
    # dash) in the figures' sans font at 600 dpi; the extension's own default is
    # restated here so the Word figures cannot silently change device.
    knitr:
      opts_chunk:
        dev: "ragg_png"
filters:
  # Centres spanners and the heads of numeric columns in every table (APA 7), in
  # the PDF and in Word; text-column heads stay flush left.
  - ../_shared/lua/apa-table-heads.lua
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
editor: source

```{r setup}
#| include: false
# =============================================================================
# Manuscript setup -- shared paths, results loading, inline-reporting helpers.
# The document is designed to render at ANY stage: before the HPC models exist it
# prints clearly-marked placeholders; once results/_pooled_*.csv are present every
# number, table and figure is populated automatically from those artefacts. This
# "render-anytime" design keeps the manuscript reproducible and prevents stale,
# hand-copied statistics (Marwick, Boettiger & Mullen, 2018,
# https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2017.1375986).
#
# Conventions of the accessors below, which are documented in comments rather than with
# roxygen blocks: each reads a table loaded once from results/ (post_tbl, retention_tbl,
# sens_tbl, conv_tbl, sdt_tbl, the decoding tables and the descriptive tables) and returns a
# string to splice into prose. When its artefact or row is missing, a bare count returns
# "NN", an estimate or sentence returns a *[...]* marker, an optional clause returns "", and
# an internal row selector returns NULL. A guard (cred_cells_guard() and its relatives)
# returns "" when the prose matches the artefact and a bold [Check: ...] marker when not.
# =============================================================================
# Figure text size, set once and inherited by every figure through les_theme(). Each
# figure is authored at the width of the text block, so nothing is scaled on placement
# and a point here is a point on the page. While several figures were authored at 8
# inches and placed in a 6.5-inch measure, the 9 pt previously set here arrived as
# roughly 7.3 pt, below what is legible in print.
LES_FIG_BASE_SIZE <- 10

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(here)
  source(here::here("_shared", "R", "00_paths.R"))
  source(here::here("_shared", "R", "05_funnel.R"))   # les_flow(), shared with Paper 2
  source(here::here("paper_1_transfer", "scripts", "_config.R"))
  # The house style shared with Paper 2 (the colour registry, les_theme() and the other
  # figure helpers, the table writer les_grid_table()), the number formatters,
  # .read_csv_if(), prov(), flow_n() and pstat(), so both manuscripts report by one set
  # of rules.
  source(here::here("_shared", "R", "06_manuscript_helpers.R"))
  source(here::here("_shared", "R", "07_task_durations.R"))
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  # Stacks the electrode-cluster blocks of the ERP time-course figures, which share one
  # legend and one y-axis title.
  library(patchwork)
  has_knitr <- requireNamespace("knitr", quietly = TRUE)
  # depictr supplies the base theme that les_theme() builds on and the diverging scale
  # les_div; the categorical colours come from the registry in 06_manuscript_helpers.R.
  # Optional: if it is unavailable les_theme() falls back to theme_minimal(), consistent
  # with the render-anytime design.
  has_depictr <- requireNamespace("depictr", quietly = TRUE)
  if (has_depictr) {
    library(depictr)
    depictr_options(base_size = LES_FIG_BASE_SIZE)
  }
})

# --- Literature-composition counts (results/_literature_trend.csv, written by
# scripts/10_extract_literature_trend.R via the Scopus API). Injected inline so the
# Introduction's claim about the field's methodological balance carries no
# hand-transcribed number and updates whenever the search is re-run.
# A stratum absent from the table prints "NN"; a stratum present with no records prints 0.
lit_n <- function(stratum) {
  if (is.null(.lit_tbl) || !any(.lit_tbl$stratum == stratum)) return("NN")
  v <- sum(.lit_tbl$n[.lit_tbl$stratum == stratum], na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(v)) "NN" else as.character(v)
}
lit_years <- function() {
  if (is.null(.lit_tbl)) return("NN")
  paste0(min(.lit_tbl$year), " and ", max(.lit_tbl$year))
}
lit_ratio <- function() {
  if (is.null(.lit_tbl)) return("NN")
  a <- sum(.lit_tbl$n[.lit_tbl$stratum == "Acceptability/grammaticality judgement"], na.rm = TRUE)
  b <- sum(.lit_tbl$n[.lit_tbl$stratum == "Electrophysiology (ERP/EEG)"], na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(a) || !is.finite(b) || b == 0) return("NN")
  as.character(round(a / b))
}

# --- Load pooled artefacts written by script 05 (if they exist) --------------
.lit_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_literature_trend.csv"))  # see lit_n() below


# --- Which random-effect structure the reported results come from ------------
# "maximal" = crossed by-participant and by-item random effects, each carrying an
# intercept plus grammaticality and session slopes. That is the structure the design
# justifies, since grammaticality varies within both participants and items, and it is
# what the paper reports. "base" is the same model without the by-item grammaticality
# slope, retained and reported as a sensitivity analysis. Every accessor below routes
# through LES_P1_PRIMARY so the two can be swapped in one place rather than by editing
# call sites, and so a half-switched document is impossible.
LES_P1_PRIMARY <- "maximal"
.STRUCT_SUFFIX <- c(maximal = "_itemslope", base = "")

# The figures draw the analysis windows from the house helpers' LES_ERP_WINDOWS
# (_shared/R/06_manuscript_helpers.R), and the models use LES_P1_WINDOWS (scripts/_config.R).
# Two definitions of one fact, so the render stops if they ever disagree.
stopifnot(identical(unname(as.numeric(LES_ERP_WINDOWS$start)),
                    unname(vapply(LES_P1_WINDOWS, `[[`, 0, "min_ms"))),
          identical(unname(as.numeric(LES_ERP_WINDOWS$end)),
                    unname(vapply(LES_P1_WINDOWS, `[[`, 0, "max_ms"))))
# The last sample each window includes, for the Method ("498, 598 and 898").
win_upper_bounds <- function() {
  b <- unname(vapply(LES_P1_WINDOWS, `[[`, 0, "max_ms"))
  paste0(paste(utils::head(b, -1), collapse = ", "), " and ", utils::tail(b, 1))
}

# Every tag that marks an ERP fit as a variant of the reported one: the weak-prior set, the
# robustness arm without the reprocessed records, the retention-free refits, and the
# retired mis-filter-retained and diversity variants, which a pooled table written before
# their retirement may still hold, and the accuracy refits with the reaction-time screen
# (and the retired refits without it, from when the screen was primary), which no ERP id
# carries but which the same test keeps out of any accuracy accessor that uses it. The
# accessors that count, range or tabulate the reported
# fits (cred_cells, cred_cells_guard, pd_range, itemslope_width_ratio, the forest plot and
# the retention table) exclude it in one place, matching the tag anywhere in the id, so a
# variant can never enter a reported count whatever order its tags compose in.
.LES_VARIANT_RE <- "_(weakprior|exclreproc|retfree|keepmisfiltered|diversity|rtscreen|nortscreen)(_|$)"
.is_variant <- function(model) grepl(.LES_VARIANT_RE, model)

# Resolve a bare ERP cell id to the primary structure's model id. Ids that already
# name a variant explicitly (a weak-prior, robustness or retention-free fit, or an
# already-suffixed cell) are returned untouched, so a call site can still reference a
# specific fit.
.mid <- function(model_id) {
  if (!grepl("^erp_", model_id)) return(model_id)                       # accuracy models
  if (grepl(.LES_VARIANT_RE, model_id) || grepl("_itemslope$", model_id)) return(model_id)
  paste0(model_id, .STRUCT_SUFFIX[[LES_P1_PRIMARY]])
}

.fitmeta_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_pooled_fit_metadata.csv"))

# Participants in the fitted ERP models of one property, from the fit records. The
# flow count is taken from the same single-trial data (00_extract_participants.R). A
# participant without the L1-dominance score is kept with the score set to the participant
# mean (step 01), so the two counts should agree; the modelled N is still read from the
# primary structure's informative fits, which all share one N per property, so that any
# disagreement shows. The fit records carry no "_retfree" in their model ids, so the
# retention-free refits are set aside by their retention_free column.
erp_model_n <- function(property) {
  if (is.null(.fitmeta_tbl)) return("NN")
  m <- .fitmeta_tbl[startsWith(.fitmeta_tbl$model, paste0("erp_", property, "_")) &
                      !grepl("_exclreproc", .fitmeta_tbl$model) &
                      .fitmeta_tbl$prior_set %in% "informative", , drop = FALSE]
  if ("structure" %in% names(m)) m <- m[m$structure %in% LES_P1_PRIMARY, , drop = FALSE]
  if ("retention_free" %in% names(m)) m <- m[!(m$retention_free %in% TRUE), , drop = FALSE]
  v <- unique(m$n_participants)
  if (length(v) != 1L || is.na(v)) return("NN")
  as.character(v)
}

# The Method states that the nine mis-filtered Session-3 datasets enter the models only as
# reprocessed at 0.1 Hz, never as the 1 Hz exports. That claim is about the models reported
# below, so it is checked against those models: scripts 03 and 04 record, for every fit,
# how many rows of the data they were fitted to belonged to a mis-filtered
# participant-session, and script 05 pools those records here. A marker is printed unless
# every applicable fit reports zero. An earlier version tested instead for the existence of
# results/_exclusions.csv, which the extraction scripts wrote as a side effect. That was
# unsound: re-running an extraction created the file even when the fitted models being
# reported were older than the exclusion, so the marker cleared while the numbers were
# stale. Keying on the fits themselves cannot fail that way. The decision rule lives in
# les_p1_misfilter_status() (scripts/_config.R), beside the helpers it audits, and
# scripts/test_exclusion_guard.R tests that function directly.
misfilter_status <- function() {
  why <- les_p1_misfilter_status(.fitmeta_tbl, LES_P1_PRIMARY)
  if (nzchar(why)) paste0(" **[Pending: ", why,
                          "; re-run the extraction and model fits to bring the reported",
                          " results into line.]**") else ""
}

# Computational provenance recorded at fit time by _shared/R/04_provenance.R, so the
# reported versions are those of the run that produced these results rather than of the
# machine rendering the document.
.prov_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_provenance.csv"))   # read by prov()
# The decoding job writes its own small provenance record (hpc/08_decoding.slurm), with the
# seed and permutation settings it actually exported. The ERP fitting run's record carries a
# default for the decoding seed that no decoding job set, so the decoding value is read from
# the decoding record and not from the ERP one.
.dprov_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_decoding_provenance.csv"))
prov_dec <- function(component, fallback = "*[value pending a decoding run]*") {
  if (is.null(.dprov_tbl)) return(fallback)
  r <- .dprov_tbl[.dprov_tbl$component == component, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(r) != 1 || is.na(r$version[1])) return(fallback)
  as.character(r$version[1])
}
conv_tbl      <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_pooled_convergence.csv"))
# Number of fitted models whose id matches a pattern, for the composition sentence in the
# convergence appendix, so the breakdown cannot drift from the injected total.
conv_n <- function(pattern) {
  if (is.null(conv_tbl)) return("NN")
  as.character(sum(grepl(pattern, conv_tbl$model)))
}
# The YAML abstract cannot hold inline R, so the one sample count it types (65 learners
# trained) is checked here against the sample flow, and a mismatch prints a visible marker
# in the Participants section.
abstract_guard <- function() {
  n <- flow_n("enrolled")
  if (identical(n, "NN") || identical(n, "65")) return("")
  sprintf(" **[Check: the abstract says 65 learners were trained; the sample flow now gives %s.]**", n)
}

# Whether every cell of the informative-prior grid met the convergence criteria under both
# random-effect structures, read from the pooled diagnostics instead of typed.
struct_conv_sentence <- function() {
  if (is.null(conv_tbl)) return("*[convergence of the two structures pending]*")
  g <- conv_tbl[grepl("^erp_.*_(lateral|midline)(_itemslope)?$", conv_tbl$model), , drop = FALSE]
  n_max <- sum(grepl("_itemslope$", g$model)); n_base <- nrow(g) - n_max
  p_max <- sum(g$passed[grepl("_itemslope$", g$model)] %in% TRUE)
  p_base <- sum(g$passed[!grepl("_itemslope$", g$model)] %in% TRUE)
  if (n_max == p_max && n_base == p_base && n_max == n_base)
    return(sprintf("All %s cells met the same convergence criteria under both.",
                   if (n_max == 18L) "eighteen" else n_max))
  sprintf("Under the maximal structure %d of %d cells, and under the simpler one %d of %d, met the convergence criteria.",
          p_max, n_max, p_base, n_base)
}
# The accuracy sensitivity refits, counted and described from the pooled diagnostics, so the
# convergence appendix names only the variants that have been fitted and pooled.
acc_refits_sentence <- function() {
  if (is.null(conv_tbl)) return("*[accuracy refit count pending]*")
  m <- conv_tbl$model[startsWith(conv_tbl$model, "accuracy_")]
  kinds <- c(maxranef = "_maxranef$", byitem = "(?<!_maxranef)_byitem$",
             both = "_maxranef_byitem$", diversity = "_diversity$",
             rtscreen = "_rtscreen$")
  n <- vapply(kinds, function(p) sum(grepl(p, m, perl = TRUE)), 0L)
  if (!sum(n)) return("")
  desc <- c(maxranef = "with a by-participant grammaticality $\\times$ session slope",
            byitem = "with the crossed by-item term",
            both = "with both",
            diversity = paste("with the questionnaire's multilingual language diversity score",
                              "as a between-participant covariate"),
            rtscreen = "with the reaction-time screen of the earlier preprocessing")[n > 0]
  joined <- if (length(desc) == 1L) desc else
    paste0(paste(utils::head(desc, -1), collapse = ", "), " and ", utils::tail(desc, 1))
  reported <- any(n[c("maxranef", "byitem", "both", "rtscreen")] > 0)
  paste0("A further ", sum(n), " accuracy refits were run as sensitivity analyses, each ",
         "property refitted ", joined, ".",
         if (reported && n[["diversity"]] > 0)
           " Estimates from all but the diversity refit appear alongside the signal-detection results."
         else if (reported) " Their estimates appear alongside the signal-detection results."
         else "")
}
# Smallest bulk or tail ESS over all parameters of all fitted models. The Method used to
# characterise the realised sampling as "substantially above" the ESS floor. That was true
# of the grid as first fitted and stopped being true when the retention-free refits joined
# the pool, without anything recomputing it, so the characterisation is replaced by the
# figure itself and taken from the artefact.
conv_min_ess <- function(which = c("bulk", "tail")) {
  which <- match.arg(which)
  col <- paste0("min_ess_", which)
  if (is.null(conv_tbl) || !col %in% names(conv_tbl)) return("NN")
  format(round(min(conv_tbl[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)), big.mark = ",")
}

# Fits run longer than the defaults stated in the Method, read from the per-fit records
# (iter_warmup, iter_sampling; written from the fitted object by les_p1_write_fit_meta).
# A record without those fields predates them and ran the defaults, since no override
# existed before them (_shared/R/01_bayesian_settings.R). Returns "" when every fit ran
# the defaults, so the sentence appears only when it is true.
iter_exceptions <- function(warmup = LES_ITER_WARMUP_DEFAULT, sampling = LES_ITER_SAMPLING_DEFAULT) {
  m <- .fitmeta_tbl
  if (is.null(m) || !all(c("iter_warmup", "iter_sampling") %in% names(m))) return("")
  x <- m[(!is.na(m$iter_warmup) & m$iter_warmup != warmup) |
         (!is.na(m$iter_sampling) & m$iter_sampling != sampling), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(x)) return("")
  # Labels in the terms Table D1 uses: property, window, macroregion, structure, prior.
  .lab <- function(tag) {
    props <- c(gender_agreement = "gender agreement",
               differential_object_marking = "differential object marking",
               verb_object_number_agreement = "verb–object number agreement")
    m <- regmatches(tag, regexec(paste0("^erp_(", paste(names(props), collapse = "|"),
                                        ")_([0-9]+)_([0-9]+)_(lateral|midline)(.*)$"), tag))[[1]]
    if (length(m) != 6L) return(sub("^erp_", "", tag))
    t <- m[6]
    paste0(props[[m[2]]], ", ", m[3], "–", m[4], " ms, ", m[5], ", ",
           if (grepl("itemslope", t)) "maximal" else "base", " structure, ",
           if (grepl("retfree", t)) "retention-free" else if (grepl("weakprior", t)) "weak prior"
           else "informative prior",
           if (grepl("exclreproc", t)) ", reprocessed excluded" else "")
  }
  what <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(x)), function(i) {
    tag <- if ("model_tag" %in% names(x)) x$model_tag[i] else x$model[i]
    sprintf("%s (%s warm-up and %s sampling iterations per chain)", .lab(tag),
            format(x$iter_warmup[i], big.mark = ","), format(x$iter_sampling[i], big.mark = ","))
  }, character(1))
  paste0(" ", if (nrow(x) == 1L) "One fit was" else sprintf("%d fits were", nrow(x)),
         " run longer, with the same seed and control settings, because ",
         if (nrow(x) == 1L) "its" else "their", " first run missed the $\\widehat{R}$ criterion ",
         "[@vehtari2021]: ", paste(what, collapse = "; "), ".")
}
LES_ITER_WARMUP_DEFAULT   <- 2000L
LES_ITER_SAMPLING_DEFAULT <- 8000L
post_tbl      <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_pooled_posterior_summaries.csv"))
retention_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_retention_contrasts.csv"))
sens_tbl      <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_prior_sensitivity.csv"))
results_ready <- !is.null(post_tbl)
# The ERP forest (fig-erp-forest) needs the ERP rows of the posterior summaries, which a
# draft can withhold while keeping the accuracy rows. Defined here because knitr evaluates
# the chunk's fig-height before the chunk runs.
erp_forest_ready <- results_ready && any(grepl("^erp_", post_tbl$model))

# The PI-facing group displays use a new, participant-balanced schema. Old pooled
# grand-average CSVs must never be mistaken for the requested group plots merely because
# their file names still match. Check the headers and require all six property x
# macroregion outputs, the six paired-window files, and the behavioural table.
.has_csv_schema <- function(files, required, n_expected = length(files)) {
  if (length(files) != n_expected || !length(files)) return(FALSE)
  all(vapply(files, function(path) {
    header <- tryCatch(names(utils::read.csv(path, nrows = 1,
                                             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)),
                       error = function(e) character())
    all(required %in% header)
  }, logical(1)))
}
.group_ga_files <- sort(list.files(paper1_results(),
                                   pattern = "^_grand_average_.*\\.csv$",
                                   full.names = TRUE), method = "radix")
.group_dw_files <- sort(list.files(paper1_results(),
                                   pattern = "^_difference_wave_.*\\.csv$",
                                   full.names = TRUE), method = "radix")
.group_topo_files <- sort(list.files(
  paper1_results(), pattern = "^_electrode_window_difference_.*\\.csv$",
  full.names = TRUE), method = "radix")
.group_sdt_path <- paper1_results("_accuracy_sdt_by_language.csv")
# The displays are drawn only from the September 2026 extraction, which baseline-corrects
# within participant, writes violation-minus-control differences and adds the pooled
# session. Its files are the only ones that carry the "pooled" session and a difference-wave
# companion, so the check below cannot be satisfied by the earlier, uncorrected outputs.
.pooled_present <- function(files) {
  length(files) > 0 && all(vapply(files, function(f) {
    s <- tryCatch(utils::read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)$session, error = function(e) NULL)
    any(s %in% "pooled")
  }, logical(1)))
}
group_figures_ready <-
  .has_csv_schema(.group_ga_files,
                  c("mini_language", "session", "mean_amp", "se_amp",
                    "n_participants"), 6L) &&
  .has_csv_schema(.group_dw_files,
                  c("mini_language", "session", "mean_difference", "se_difference",
                    "n_participants"), 6L) &&
  .has_csv_schema(.group_topo_files,
                  c("mini_language", "session", "window", "mean_difference",
                    "n_participants"), 6L) &&
  file.exists(.group_sdt_path) &&
  .has_csv_schema(.group_sdt_path,
                  c("mini_language", "session", "measure", "mean_value", "ci_low",
                    "ci_high", "n_participants"), 1L) &&
  .pooled_present(.group_topo_files)

# --- Signal-detection reading of the accuracy models ------------------------------
# The accuracy models regress `correct` on grammaticality, session and language, which
# makes the grammaticality terms response-bias terms and the remaining terms sensitivity
# terms (DeCarlo, 1998; see scripts/04_fit_brms_accuracy.R). Script 05 derives both
# quantities per language and session from the posterior draws and writes
# results/_accuracy_sdt_contrasts.csv, which the accessors below read. Sensitivity is on the
# logit scale (d_L); the criterion c_L is negative for a readiness to answer "grammatical".
sdt_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_accuracy_sdt_contrasts.csv"))
sdt_desc_tbl <- .read_csv_if(.group_sdt_path)
.sdt_row <- function(property, measure, contrast, session, language = NULL,
                     model = paste0("accuracy_", property)) {
  if (is.null(sdt_tbl)) return(NULL)
  k <- sdt_tbl$model == model & sdt_tbl$measure == measure &
       sdt_tbl$contrast == contrast & as.character(sdt_tbl$session) == session
  if (!is.null(language)) k <- k & sdt_tbl$mini_language == language
  r <- sdt_tbl[k, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(r) != 1) NULL else r
}
# Inline reporter, e.g. report_sdt("gender_agreement", "criterion", "language_difference",
# "6"). Differences and changes print as Delta; group values as d_L or c_L.
report_sdt <- function(property, measure, contrast, session, language = NULL,
                       model = paste0("accuracy_", property)) {
  if (is.null(sdt_tbl)) return("*[pending signal-detection summaries]*")
  r <- .sdt_row(property, measure, contrast, session, language, model)
  if (is.null(r)) return("*[signal-detection contrast not found]*")
  sym <- if (contrast == "value") {
    if (measure == "sensitivity") "d_L" else "c_L"
  } else "\\Delta"
  d <- .les_digits(r$median, r$ci_low, r$ci_high)
  # A bound still within rounding of zero at .les_digits()'s ceiling keeps its sign, since
  # apa_num() prints it as an unsigned zero, which would contradict a credible interval.
  .num <- function(x) {
    s <- apa_num(x, digits = d)
    if (is.finite(x) && x < 0 && !startsWith(s, "-")) paste0("-", s) else s
  }
  sprintf("$%s = %s$, 95%% CrI $[%s, %s]$, $%s$", sym,
          .num(r$median), .num(r$ci_low), .num(r$ci_high), .pd_math(r$pd))
}
# The Monte Carlo standard errors of the signal-detection contrasts' interval bounds
# (mcse_low, mcse_high, written by 05), as the size of the error a rerun can move a bound by.
sdt_mcse_sentence <- function() {
  if (is.null(sdt_tbl) || !all(c("mcse_low", "mcse_high") %in% names(sdt_tbl))) {
    return("*[Monte Carlo standard errors pending a run of 05]*")
  }
  m <- c(sdt_tbl$mcse_low, sdt_tbl$mcse_high)
  sprintf(paste0("For the signal-detection contrasts, the Monte Carlo standard error of an ",
                 "interval bound had a median of %s and a maximum of %s on the logit scale."),
          apa_num(stats::median(m), digits = 3), apa_num(max(m), digits = 3))
}
# Whether a signal-detection contrast is credible (interval excludes zero); NA if absent.
sdt_credible <- function(property, measure, contrast, session, language = NULL,
                         model = paste0("accuracy_", property)) {
  r <- .sdt_row(property, measure, contrast, session, language, model)
  if (is.null(r)) NA else (r$ci_low > 0 || r$ci_high < 0)
}
# The sessions, in order, at which a language difference in `measure` is credible, as
# prose ("Sessions 3, 4 and 6"), or "no session" when none is. Reported rather than typed
# so the sentence tracks the refits.
sdt_credible_sessions <- function(property, measure, model = paste0("accuracy_", property)) {
  if (is.null(sdt_tbl)) return("*[pending signal-detection summaries]*")
  r <- sdt_tbl[sdt_tbl$model == model & sdt_tbl$measure == measure &
                 sdt_tbl$contrast == "language_difference" &
                 sdt_tbl$session %in% as.character(LES_ERP_SESSIONS), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(r)) return("*[signal-detection contrast not found]*")
  s <- r$session[r$ci_low > 0 | r$ci_high < 0]
  s <- as.character(sort(as.integer(s)))
  if (!length(s)) return("no session")
  if (length(s) == 1L) return(paste("Session", s))
  paste0("Sessions ", paste(s[-length(s)], collapse = ", "), " and ", s[length(s)])
}
# A change from a property's first to last session in one group, as a verb phrase with its
# estimate: "declined credibly ($\Delta$ = ...)", "rose credibly (...)" or "did not change
# credibly (...)". For the criterion, a fall is a shift towards answering "grammatical".
sdt_change_phrase <- function(property, measure, language,
                              model = paste0("accuracy_", property)) {
  # Each property's first measured session (see @fig-design).
  first <- c(gender_agreement = "2", differential_object_marking = "3",
             verb_object_number_agreement = "4")[[property]]
  span <- paste(first, "6", sep = "->")
  r <- .sdt_row(property, measure, "change_first_to_last", span, language, model)
  if (is.null(r)) return("*[signal-detection contrast pending]*")
  est <- report_sdt(property, measure, "change_first_to_last", span, language, model)
  verb <- if (r$ci_high < 0) {
    if (measure == "criterion") "became credibly more liberal" else "declined credibly"
  } else if (r$ci_low > 0) {
    if (measure == "criterion") "became credibly more conservative" else "rose credibly"
  } else "did not change credibly"
  paste0(verb, " (", est, ")")
}
# Across the three properties, where a between-language difference in `measure` is credible:
# a clause such as "at no session for any property" or "for gender agreement at Sessions 3,
# 4 and 6". Used so the claim of a (non-)difference is computed, not typed.
sdt_language_clause_model <- function(measure, tag) {
  sdt_language_clause(measure, tag = tag, properties = "gender_agreement")
}
sdt_language_clause <- function(measure, tag = "", properties = names(LES_P1_PROPERTIES)) {
  if (is.null(sdt_tbl)) return("*[pending signal-detection summaries]*")
  parts <- vapply(properties, function(p) {
    s <- sdt_credible_sessions(p, measure, model = paste0("accuracy_", p, tag))
    if (identical(s, "no session") || startsWith(s, "*")) "" else
      paste0("for ", LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_PROSE[[p]], " at ", s)
  }, "")
  parts <- parts[nzchar(parts)]
  if (!length(parts)) {
    return(if (length(properties) == 1L) "at no session" else "at no session for any property")
  }
  if (length(parts) == 1L) return(parts)
  paste0(paste(parts[-length(parts)], collapse = "; "), "; and ", parts[length(parts)])
}

# --- Raw-data descriptives: participant flow, demographics and ERP trial
# retention, written by scripts 00_extract_participants.R and
# 00c_extract_erp_retention.R. Injected inline so no count, demographic or
# retention figure is transcribed by hand (the drift that leaves the two papers
# disagreeing on a count is thereby impossible).
flow_tbl    <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_sample_flow.csv"))
parts_tbl   <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_participants.csv"))
erp_ret_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_erp_trial_retention.csv"))
task_duration_home <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_task_durations_home.csv"))
task_duration_lab  <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_task_durations_lab.csv"))
# Three further descriptives that were typed into the Method until the extraction
# scripts were extended to write them (00_extract_participants.R,
# 00c_extract_erp_retention.R and 02_extract_accuracy.R). Each sentence below prints a
# marked fallback until its artefact exists, so a typed value can never outlive the data.
other_lang_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_participants_other_languages.csv"))
mis_share_tbl  <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_misfiltered_share.csv"))

# Languages reported beyond Norwegian and English: how many participants, and the two
# most often named.
other_lang_sentence <- function() {
  n <- pstat("n_other_language", "value", 0)
  if (identical(n, "NN") || is.null(other_lang_tbl) || !nrow(other_lang_tbl)) {
    return(paste0("Some participants also reported knowledge of a further language, most ",
                  "often German or Spanish, which the design did not screen out (see ",
                  "Limitations). *[count pending the participant extraction]*"))
  }
  # The two most often named, ordered here rather than relying on the file's row order;
  # alphabetical order breaks a tie.
  o <- other_lang_tbl[order(-other_lang_tbl$n_participants, other_lang_tbl$language), ]
  top <- utils::head(o$language, 2)
  paste0(n, " of the ", pstat("n_lhq3", "value", 0), " also reported knowledge of at least ",
         "one further language, most often ", paste(top, collapse = " or "), ". Several of ",
         "the languages named mark grammatical gender or case, and the design did not ",
         "screen them out (see Limitations).")
}

# Share of the retained Session 3 trials held by the nine reprocessed datasets, per
# property recorded at that session. The reprocessing keeps exactly the trials of the 1 Hz
# exports, so the share is the same before and after it.
misfilter_share_sentence <- function() {
  if (is.null(mis_share_tbl) || !nrow(mis_share_tbl)) {
    return(paste0("The reprocessed datasets hold about a sixth of the Session 3 trials in ",
                  "both the gender-agreement and the differential-object-marking analyses ",
                  "*[share pending the retention extraction]*."))
  }
  lab <- LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_PROSE
  m <- mis_share_tbl[order(mis_share_tbl$session,
                           match(mis_share_tbl$grammatical_property, names(lab))), ]
  m <- m[m$n_datasets_misfiltered > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  # The mis-filtered datasets now span two sessions, so each share names its session.
  parts <- sprintf("%s%% of the retained Session %s %s trials", apa_num(m$share_pct, digits = 1),
                   m$session, unname(lab[m$grammatical_property]))
  paste0("The reprocessed datasets hold ",
         if (length(parts) > 1)
           paste0(paste(utils::head(parts, -1), collapse = ", "), " and ", utils::tail(parts, 1))
         else parts, ".")
}

# The trigger-rule check of protocol Amendment 5
# (scripts/eeg_reconstruction/checks/trigger_check.py), pulled from the store's
# eeg_reprocessing/trigger_check/results/trigger_check_cells.csv. Its primary rows compare
# every discarded lag with the kept trials; the "lag 6 only" rows are a sensitivity set and
# are not reported. NULL until the check has run, when the sentence prints a marker.
trig_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_trigger_check_cells.csv"))
# pandas writes logicals as "True"/"False", which read.csv leaves as text.
if (!is.null(trig_tbl)) trig_tbl$passes <- as.logical(trig_tbl$passes)
.trig_primary <- function() {
  if (is.null(trig_tbl)) return(NULL)
  d <- trig_tbl[trig_tbl$discarded_set == "all lags other than 5", , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(d)) d else NULL
}
trigger_check_sentence <- function() {
  d <- .trig_primary()
  if (is.null(d)) {
    return(paste0("*[The check runs once the raw signal of the four Session 2 comparison ",
                  "recordings is in place; its result will appear here.]*"))
  }
  lab <- LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_PROSE
  n_pass <- sum(d$passes)
  words <- c("none", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight",
             "nine", "ten", "eleven", "twelve")
  .w <- function(n) if (n < length(words)) words[n + 1] else as.character(n)
  far <- d[which.max(pmax(abs(d$ci90_low), abs(d$ci90_high))), ]
  .cell <- function(r) sprintf("%s, %s ms, %s", unname(lab[r$property]),
                               sub("_", "--", r$window), r$macroregion)
  dg <- function(x) apa_num(x, digits = 2)
  .est <- function(r) sprintf("$D = %s$ µV, 90%% CI $[%s, %s]$", dg(r$D_int), dg(r$ci90_low),
                              dg(r$ci90_high))
  head <- if (n_pass == nrow(d)) sprintf("All %s cells passed.", .w(nrow(d))) else
    sprintf("%s of the %s cells passed.", tools::toTitleCase(.w(n_pass)), .w(nrow(d)))
  # Cells whose interval excludes zero, where the two sets of trials differ, as distinct from
  # cells that fail only because their interval is too wide to bound the difference.
  ex <- d[d$ci90_low > 0 | d$ci90_high < 0, , drop = FALSE]
  ex_txt <- if (!nrow(ex)) {
    " No interval excluded zero, so every cell that failed did so because its interval reached beyond the bound."
  } else {
    sprintf(paste0(" The interval excluded zero in %s (%s), where the discarded trials carried the ",
                   "more %s ungrammatical-minus-grammatical difference. Across %s cells, %s such ",
                   "interval%s would be expected on average at the 90%% level if the two sets of ",
                   "trials did not differ."),
            if (nrow(ex) == 1L) .cell(ex) else paste(.w(nrow(ex)), "cells"),
            if (nrow(ex) == 1L) .est(ex) else "see @tbl-trigger-check",
            if (all(ex$D_int < 0)) "negative" else if (all(ex$D_int > 0)) "positive" else "extreme",
            .w(nrow(d)), apa_num(0.1 * nrow(d), digits = 1), if (0.1 * nrow(d) == 1) "" else "s")
  }
  sprintf(paste0("%s Across the %s recordings, %s%% of the eligible grammatical and ",
                 "ungrammatical words had been discarded.%s The interval reaching furthest from ",
                 "zero was that of %s (%s), which would shift the analysed contrast by $%s$ µV at ",
                 "its median. Every cell is given in @tbl-trigger-check."),
          head, .w(max(d$n_recordings)), apa_num(100 * stats::weighted.mean(d$share_discarded,
                                                                            d$n_kept + d$n_discarded), digits = 0),
          ex_txt, .cell(far), .est(far), dg(far$implied_shift))
}
# The limitation Amendment 5 requires when the trigger-rule check fails: how many cells it
# could not bound, and, where an interval excludes zero, which way the omission biases the
# analysed contrast. Empty when every cell passes.
trigger_limit_sentence <- function() {
  d <- .trig_primary()
  if (is.null(d) || all(d$passes)) return("")
  words <- c("none", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine",
             "ten", "eleven", "twelve")
  .w <- function(n) if (n < length(words)) words[n + 1] else as.character(n)
  ex <- d[d$ci90_low > 0 | d$ci90_high < 0, , drop = FALSE]
  share <- stats::weighted.mean(d$share_discarded, d$n_kept + d$n_discarded)
  out <- sprintf(paste0(" The trigger rule that segmented the exports discarded %s%% of the ",
                        "critical words, and the check of whether the discarded words differ from ",
                        "the kept ones passed in %s of its %s cells (@tbl-trigger-check), so ",
                        "elsewhere it cannot exclude an omission that shifts a grammaticality ",
                        "contrast by more than %s µV."),
                 apa_num(100 * share, digits = 0), .w(sum(d$passes)), .w(nrow(d)),
                 apa_num(0.362 * 0.91, digits = 2))
  if (nrow(ex) == 1L && ex$D_int < 0) {
    out <- paste0(out, sprintf(paste0(" In the one cell where the two sets differed (%s, %s ms, ",
                                      "%s), the discarded words carried the more negative ",
                                      "difference, so the analysed contrast there understates ",
                                      "any violation negativity."),
                               unname(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_PROSE[ex$property]), sub("_", "--", ex$window),
                               ex$macroregion))
  } else if (nrow(ex)) {
    out <- paste0(out, " **[Check: describe the cells whose interval excludes zero.]**")
  }
  out
}

# The refits with the crossed by-item term (LES_P1_ACC_ITEM=1; tags _byitem and
# _maxranef_byitem), reported beside the _maxranef refit. Each by-item refit is compared,
# contrast by contrast over all three properties, with the refit that has the same
# by-participant structure and no item term, and the sentence names every contrast whose
# credibility the item term changes. A missing model prints a marker rather than being
# read as "no change".
.has_sdt_model <- function(model) !is.null(sdt_tbl) && any(sdt_tbl$model == model)
.BYITEM_PAIRS <- c("_byitem" = "", "_maxranef_byitem" = "_maxranef")
.byitem_comparison <- function() {
  props <- names(LES_P1_PROPERTIES)
  need <- c(outer(paste0("accuracy_", props), c(names(.BYITEM_PAIRS), .BYITEM_PAIRS), paste0))
  if (!all(vapply(need, .has_sdt_model, logical(1)))) return(NULL)
  d <- sdt_tbl[sdt_tbl$contrast != "value", , drop = FALSE]
  k <- c("measure", "contrast", "mini_language", "session")
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(props, function(p) do.call(rbind, lapply(names(.BYITEM_PAIRS), function(tg) {
    m <- merge(d[d$model == paste0("accuracy_", p, .BYITEM_PAIRS[[tg]]), ],
               d[d$model == paste0("accuracy_", p, tg), ], by = k, suffixes = c("", "_item"))
    if (nrow(m)) { m$property <- p; m$tag <- tg }
    m
  }))))
  .cred <- function(lo, hi) lo > 0 | hi < 0
  out$cred <- .cred(out$ci_low, out$ci_high)
  out$cred_item <- .cred(out$ci_low_item, out$ci_high_item)
  out
}
# A contrast row as a noun phrase: "the Mini-English group's change in criterion between
# Sessions 4 and 6 for verb--object number agreement".
.sdt_contrast_label <- function(r) {
  prop <- LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_PROSE[[r$property]]
  span <- strsplit(as.character(r$session), "->", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  between <- if (length(span) == 2L) sprintf("between Sessions %s and %s", span[1], span[2]) else ""
  if (r$contrast == "language_difference") {
    at <- if (r$session == "average") "averaged over sessions" else paste("at Session", r$session)
    sprintf("the difference between the groups' %s for %s %s", r$measure, prop, at)
  } else if (grepl("_language_difference$", r$contrast)) {
    sprintf("the difference between the groups' changes in %s %s for %s", r$measure, between, prop)
  } else {
    sprintf("the %s group's change in %s %s for %s", r$mini_language, r$measure, between, prop)
  }
}
# Changed contrasts as one list of clauses: two joined by ", and", three or more by
# semicolons, since each clause is a long noun phrase with its verb.
.clause_list <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) <= 2L) return(paste(x, collapse = ", and "))
  paste0(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = "; "), "; and ", x[length(x)])
}
byitem_sentence <- function() {
  m <- .byitem_comparison()
  if (is.null(m)) {
    return("*[The refits with the crossed by-item term are pending; their result will appear here.]*")
  }
  flips <- m[m$cred != m$cred_item, , drop = FALSE]
  n_words <- c("none", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six")
  .n <- function(n) if (n < length(n_words)) n_words[n + 1] else as.character(n)
  n_con <- nrow(m) / length(.BYITEM_PAIRS)
  head <- sprintf(paste0("Refitted with the ERP models' crossed by-item term as well, the %s ",
                         "signal-detection contrasts of the three properties, compared under ",
                         "each by-participant structure in turn, "),
                  if (n_con == round(n_con)) n_con else nrow(m))
  body <- if (!nrow(flips)) {
    "all kept their credibility."
  } else {
    gender_note <- if (!any(flips$property == "gender_agreement"))
      ", none of them for gender agreement" else ""
    # How far the interval that excludes zero stays from it, in each changed contrast.
    margin <- ifelse(flips$cred, pmin(abs(flips$ci_low), abs(flips$ci_high)),
                     pmin(abs(flips$ci_low_item), abs(flips$ci_high_item)))
    descr <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(flips)), function(i) {
      r <- flips[i, ]
      sprintf("%s %s (%s)", .sdt_contrast_label(r),
              if (r$cred_item) "became credible" else "ceased to be credible",
              if (r$tag == "_byitem") "with the reported by-participant structure" else
                "with the added slope")
    }, "")
    listing <- .clause_list(descr)
    sprintf(paste0("kept their credibility in all but %s of the %d comparisons%s: %s. In each, ",
                   "the interval that excluded zero did so by no more than %s on the logit scale."),
            .n(nrow(flips)), nrow(m), gender_note, listing,
            apa_num(ceiling(100 * max(margin)) / 100, digits = 2))
  }
  paste0(head, body, " With both terms, the difference between the gender-agreement groups' ",
         "criteria averaged over sessions was ",
         report_sdt("gender_agreement", "criterion", "language_difference", "average",
                    model = "accuracy_gender_agreement_maxranef_byitem"), ".")
}
# The accuracy models refitted with the legacy reaction-time screen (LES_P1_ACC_RT_SCREEN=1,
# tag _rtscreen), the sensitivity analysis since 19 October 2026 (ISSUES.md G06-03). From 17
# to 19 October the roles were the other way round: the screened fits were reported and an
# unscreened refit was the sensitivity analysis. As for the by-item refits, each property's
# screened refit is compared with its reported fit contrast by contrast, and the sentence
# names every contrast whose credibility the screen decides. A marker replaces it until all
# three refits and the variant's filter file are pulled, and another if the screened sample
# is not the reported trials less those the screen removes.
.rt_comparison <- function() {
  props <- names(LES_P1_PROPERTIES)
  need <- c(paste0("accuracy_", props), paste0("accuracy_", props, "_rtscreen"))
  if (!all(vapply(need, .has_sdt_model, logical(1)))) return(NULL)
  d <- sdt_tbl[sdt_tbl$contrast != "value", , drop = FALSE]
  k <- c("measure", "contrast", "mini_language", "session")
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(props, function(p) {
    m <- merge(d[d$model == paste0("accuracy_", p), ],
               d[d$model == paste0("accuracy_", p, "_rtscreen"), ], by = k,
               suffixes = c("", "_sc"))
    if (nrow(m)) m$property <- p
    m
  }))
  .cred <- function(lo, hi) lo > 0 | hi < 0
  out$cred <- .cred(out$ci_low, out$ci_high)
  out$cred_sc <- .cred(out$ci_low_sc, out$ci_high_sc)
  out
}
rt_screen_sentence <- function() {
  m <- .rt_comparison()
  if (is.null(m) || is.null(.rt_tbl_sc) || is.null(.rt_tbl)) {
    return("*[The refits with the reaction-time screen are pending; their result will appear here.]*")
  }
  n_all <- .rt_tbl$n_kept[1]; n_sc <- .rt_tbl_sc$n_kept[1]
  if (!isTRUE(n_all > n_sc) || !identical(.rt_tbl$n_valid_trials[1], .rt_tbl_sc$n_valid_trials[1])) {
    return(paste0(" **[Check: the screened accuracy data are not the reported trials less those ",
                  "the screen removes. Rerun 02, and 02 under LES_P1_ACC_RT_SCREEN=1.]**"))
  }
  flips <- m[m$cred != m$cred_sc, , drop = FALSE]
  n_words <- c("none", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six")
  .n <- function(n) if (n < length(n_words)) n_words[n + 1] else as.character(n)
  # The Results lead-in already says the models were refitted with the screen.
  head <- sprintf(paste0("On the %s judgement trials the screen keeps (%s fewer), the %d ",
                         "signal-detection contrasts of the three properties "),
                  format(n_sc, big.mark = ","), format(n_all - n_sc, big.mark = ","), nrow(m))
  body <- if (!nrow(flips)) {
    "all kept their credibility."
  } else {
    gender_note <- if (!any(flips$property == "gender_agreement"))
      ", none of them for gender agreement" else ""
    margin <- ifelse(flips$cred, pmin(abs(flips$ci_low), abs(flips$ci_high)),
                     pmin(abs(flips$ci_low_sc), abs(flips$ci_high_sc)))
    descr <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(flips)), function(i) {
      r <- flips[i, ]
      sprintf("%s %s", .sdt_contrast_label(r),
              if (r$cred_sc) "became credible" else "ceased to be credible")
    }, "")
    listing <- .clause_list(descr)
    sprintf(paste0("kept their credibility in all but %s%s: %s. In each, the interval that ",
                   "excluded zero did so by no more than %s on the logit scale."),
            .n(nrow(flips)), gender_note, listing,
            apa_num(ceiling(100 * max(margin)) / 100, digits = 2))
  }
  # The population-level terms the Results report for the models, compared the same way.
  terms <- .rt_term_flips()
  terms_txt <- if (is.null(terms)) "" else if (terms$n_flip == 0L)
    sprintf(" None of the %d population-level terms of the three models changed its relation to zero.",
            terms$n)
  else sprintf(" %s of the %d population-level terms of the three models changed its relation to zero.",
               tools::toTitleCase(.n(terms$n_flip)), terms$n)
  rep <- .sdt_row("gender_agreement", "criterion", "language_difference", "average")
  paste0(head, body, terms_txt, " With the screen, the difference between the ",
         "gender-agreement groups' criteria averaged over sessions was ",
         report_sdt("gender_agreement", "criterion", "language_difference", "average",
                    model = "accuracy_gender_agreement_rtscreen"),
         if (!is.null(rep)) sprintf(", against $\\Delta = %s$ without it",
                                    apa_num(rep$median, digits = .les_digits(rep$median, rep$ci_low,
                                                                             rep$ci_high))) else "",
         ".")
}
# The population-level terms whose 95% interval excludes zero in one of a property's two
# fits (reported and _rtscreen) but not the other, counted over the three properties.
# NULL while either fit is missing from the pooled summaries.
.rt_term_flips <- function(tbl = post_tbl) {
  if (is.null(tbl)) return(NULL)
  ids <- paste0("accuracy_", names(LES_P1_PROPERTIES))
  if (!all(c(ids, paste0(ids, "_rtscreen")) %in% tbl$model)) return(NULL)
  m <- do.call(rbind, lapply(ids, function(id)
    merge(tbl[tbl$model == id, ],
          tbl[tbl$model == paste0(id, "_rtscreen"), ], by = "parameter", suffixes = c("", "_sc"))))
  .cred <- function(lo, hi) lo > 0 | hi < 0
  list(n = nrow(m), n_flip = sum(.cred(m$ci_low, m$ci_high) != .cred(m$ci_low_sc, m$ci_high_sc)))
}
# The Strength-of-evidence weighing of the refit with the reaction-time screen. The
# contrasts whose credibility the screen decides are named as the results graded
# suggestive, beside what the two fits share for the gender-agreement criterion difference:
# where it is credible with the screen, how much larger it is there at each session, and
# that in both fits it is not credible at Session 2 and grows credibly between Sessions 2 and
# 6. The paragraph reads every changed gender-agreement sensitivity contrast as running
# against a Mini-Norwegian advantage and every changed contrast of another property as
# unpredicted, so a marker replaces it when a gender-agreement sensitivity contrast runs the
# other way in either fit, or when the criterion difference leaves the pattern.
rtscreen_weight_paragraph <- function() {
  m <- .rt_comparison()
  if (is.null(m)) {
    return("*[The refits with the reaction-time screen are pending; their weighing will appear here.]*")
  }
  sc <- "accuracy_gender_agreement_rtscreen"
  ss <- as.character(LES_ERP_SESSIONS)
  .ld <- function(model) lapply(ss, function(s)
    .sdt_row("gender_agreement", "criterion", "language_difference", s, model = model))
  rp <- .ld("accuracy_gender_agreement"); scr <- .ld(sc)
  .grow <- function(model) .sdt_row("gender_agreement", "criterion",
                                    "change_first_to_last_language_difference", "2->6", model = model)
  .cred <- function(r) !is.null(r) && (r$ci_low > 0 || r$ci_high < 0)
  flips <- m[m$cred != m$cred_sc, , drop = FALSE]
  gsens <- flips[flips$property == "gender_agreement" & flips$measure == "sensitivity", , drop = FALSE]
  gap <- vapply(seq_along(ss), function(i) {
    if (is.null(rp[[i]]) || is.null(scr[[i]])) NA_real_ else abs(scr[[i]]$median) - abs(rp[[i]]$median)
  }, numeric(1))
  holds <- nrow(flips) > 0L && all(gsens$median < 0 & gsens$median_sc < 0) &&
    !anyNA(gap) && all(gap > 0) && !.cred(rp[[1]]) && !.cred(scr[[1]]) &&
    .cred(.grow("accuracy_gender_agreement")) && .cred(.grow(sc))
  if (!holds) {
    return(paste0("**[Check: the refits with the reaction-time screen no longer fit the ",
                  "paragraph written for them in Strength of evidence. Revise it.]**"))
  }
  # Gender agreement first, the criterion before sensitivity, sessions before changes.
  flips <- flips[order(flips$property != "gender_agreement", flips$measure != "criterion",
                       flips$contrast != "language_difference", flips$session), , drop = FALSE]
  items <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(flips)), function(i) {
    r <- flips[i, ]
    what <- if (r$property == "gender_agreement" && r$contrast == "language_difference" &&
                r$session %in% ss) {
      if (r$measure == "criterion") sprintf("the criterion difference at Session %s", r$session) else
        sprintf("the Mini-Norwegian group's lower sensitivity at Session %s", r$session)
    } else .sdt_contrast_label(r)
    sprintf("%s, credible only %s the screen (%s)", what, if (r$cred_sc) "with" else "without",
            report_sdt(r$property, r$measure, r$contrast, r$session, language = r$mini_language,
                       model = paste0("accuracy_", r$property, if (r$cred_sc) "_rtscreen" else "")))
  }, "")
  # The screen is named in the first item; later ones refer back to it.
  items[-1] <- sub(" the screen (", " it (", items[-1], fixed = TRUE)
  n_words <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight")
  results <- if (nrow(flips) == 1L) "the result" else
    paste("the", if (nrow(flips) <= length(n_words)) n_words[nrow(flips)] else nrow(flips), "results")
  # How far the interval that excludes zero stays from it, in the fit that supports each one,
  # and the Monte Carlo standard error of that bound (05 writes it), so a margin within two
  # of them is read as one these runs do not settle.
  margin <- ifelse(flips$cred, pmin(abs(flips$ci_low), abs(flips$ci_high)),
                   pmin(abs(flips$ci_low_sc), abs(flips$ci_high_sc)))
  mc <- if (all(c("mcse_low", "mcse_high") %in% names(flips))) {
    ifelse(flips$cred,
           ifelse(abs(flips$ci_low) < abs(flips$ci_high), flips$mcse_low, flips$mcse_high),
           ifelse(abs(flips$ci_low_sc) < abs(flips$ci_high_sc), flips$mcse_low_sc, flips$mcse_high_sc))
  } else rep(NA_real_, nrow(flips))
  n_mc <- sum(margin < 2 * mc, na.rm = TRUE)
  sens_txt <- if (!nrow(gsens)) "" else
    sprintf(" The gender-agreement sensitivity difference%s against a Mini-Norwegian advantage, not towards one.",
            if (nrow(gsens) == 1L) " runs" else "s run")
  other <- unique(flips$property[flips$property != "gender_agreement"])
  other_txt <- if (!length(other)) "" else
    sprintf(" Those for %s concern %s absent from both prior languages, for which no account predicts a group difference.",
            paste(unlist(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_PROSE[other]), collapse = " and "),
            if (length(other) == 1L) "a property" else "properties")
  paste0("The refit with the reaction-time screen qualifies the gender-agreement criterion ",
         "difference in another way. With the screen, the groups' criteria differed credibly ",
         sdt_language_clause_model("criterion", "_rtscreen"), ". The difference was larger at ",
         "every session, by ", apa_num(min(gap), digits = 2), " to ",
         apa_num(max(gap), digits = 2), " on the logit scale, but as without the screen it was ",
         "not credible at Session ", ss[1], " and grew credibly between Sessions 2 and 6 (",
         report_sdt("gender_agreement", "criterion", "change_first_to_last_language_difference",
                    "2->6", model = sc),
         "). The screen therefore bears on the size of the difference more than on its course. ",
         "We report the fits without it, for the reasons given under *Grammaticality-judgement ",
         "task*, and grade as suggestive ", results, " that only one of the two fits supports: ",
         .clause_list(items), ". Each interval excluded zero, in the fit that supports it, by no ",
         "more than ", apa_num(ceiling(100 * max(margin)) / 100, digits = 2), " on the logit scale",
         if (n_mc) sprintf(paste0(", and %s by less than two Monte Carlo standard errors of ",
                                  "that bound, so these runs do not settle which side of zero %s on"),
                           if (n_mc == nrow(flips)) "every one" else paste(n_words[n_mc], "of them"),
                           if (n_mc == 1L) "it falls" else "they fall") else "",
         ".", sens_txt, other_txt)
}
# The concession on the gender-agreement sensitivity difference in the Discussion's
# misanalysis account, worded from where that difference is credible in the reported fit and
# in each refit (.SDT_REFIT_LABELS): the refits in which it is not credible at every session
# where the reported fit has it are named. The account reads the difference's direction
# (Mini-Norwegian lower), so a credible difference the other way in any fit is flagged.
.SDT_REFIT_LABELS <- c("_rtscreen" = "with the reaction-time screen",
                       "_diversity" = "with the diversity covariate",
                       "_maxranef" = "with the added slope",
                       "_byitem" = "with the by-item term",
                       "_maxranef_byitem" = "with both the added slope and the by-item term",
                       "_weakprior" = "under weak priors")
# Short phrases as one list: "a", "a and b", "a, b and c".
.and_list <- function(x) if (length(x) <= 1L) x else
  paste(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = ", "), "and", x[length(x)])
sens_difference_concession <- function() {
  s_rep <- sdt_credible_sessions("gender_agreement", "sensitivity")
  if (startsWith(s_rep, "*")) return(s_rep)
  ss <- as.character(LES_ERP_SESSIONS)
  ids <- paste0("accuracy_gender_agreement", names(.SDT_REFIT_LABELS))
  have <- vapply(ids, .has_sdt_model, logical(1))
  ids <- ids[have]; labels <- unname(.SDT_REFIT_LABELS[have])
  r <- sdt_tbl[sdt_tbl$model %in% c("accuracy_gender_agreement", ids) &
                 sdt_tbl$measure == "sensitivity" & sdt_tbl$contrast == "language_difference" &
                 sdt_tbl$session %in% ss, , drop = FALSE]
  cr <- r$ci_low > 0 | r$ci_high < 0
  if (any(cr & r$median > 0)) {
    return(paste0("**[Check: the Mini-Norwegian group is now credibly the more sensitive at some ",
                  "session. Revise this sentence.]**"))
  }
  at <- function(id) r$session[r$model == id & cr]
  words <- c("none", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six")
  .w <- function(n) if (n < length(words)) words[n + 1] else as.character(n)
  rep_at <- at("accuracy_gender_agreement")
  if (!length(rep_at)) {
    where <- labels[vapply(ids, function(id) length(at(id)) > 0, logical(1))]
    if (!length(where)) return("although that difference was not credible in the reported fit or any refit")
    return(paste0("although that difference was credible only ", .and_list(where)))
  }
  if (!length(ids)) return(paste0("which was credible only at ", s_rep))
  lost <- labels[vapply(ids, function(id) !all(rep_at %in% at(id)), logical(1))]
  if (!length(lost)) return(paste0("which was credible only at ", s_rep, ", in the reported fit and in every refit"))
  if (length(ids) == 1L) return(sprintf("which was credible only at %s, and not in the refit %s", s_rep, lost))
  if (length(lost) == length(ids)) return(sprintf("which was credible only at %s, and in none of the %s refits",
                                                  s_rep, .w(length(ids))))
  sprintf("which was credible only at %s, and not in %s of the %s refits (%s)", s_rep,
          .w(length(lost)), .w(length(ids)), .and_list(lost))
}
# The Discussion's opening statement of the gender-agreement sensitivity difference: where it
# is credible in the reported fits, and in which direction. A credible Mini-Norwegian
# advantage would contradict the sentences around it, so it is flagged.
sens_gender_clause <- function() {
  if (is.null(sdt_tbl)) return("*[pending signal-detection summaries]*")
  r <- sdt_tbl[sdt_tbl$model == "accuracy_gender_agreement" & sdt_tbl$measure == "sensitivity" &
                 sdt_tbl$contrast == "language_difference" &
                 sdt_tbl$session %in% as.character(LES_ERP_SESSIONS), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(r)) return("*[signal-detection contrast not found]*")
  cr <- r[r$ci_low > 0 | r$ci_high < 0, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(cr)) return("a group difference in sensitivity to gender agreement was credible at no session")
  if (any(cr$median > 0)) {
    return("**[Check: the Mini-Norwegian group is now credibly the more sensitive at some session. Revise this paragraph.]**")
  }
  paste0("the Mini-Norwegian group was credibly less sensitive to gender agreement only at ",
         sdt_credible_sessions("gender_agreement", "sensitivity"))
}
# Typed claims of the abstract, the Discussion and the Conclusion about the signal-detection
# results, checked against the reported fits; each failure is named in a visible marker.
# The claims: no session at which the Mini-Norwegian group is credibly the more sensitive to
# gender agreement, and its sensitivity estimate the lower at every session; no credible
# sensitivity difference for the two control properties; and a criterion difference that is
# not credible at Session 2, credible at the last two sessions ("in the later sessions") and
# averaged over sessions, with the Mini-Norwegian group the more liberal.
sdt_claims_guard <- function() {
  if (is.null(sdt_tbl) || !.has_sdt_model("accuracy_gender_agreement")) return("")
  ss <- as.character(LES_ERP_SESSIONS)
  ld <- function(p, measure) {
    r <- sdt_tbl[sdt_tbl$model == paste0("accuracy_", p) & sdt_tbl$measure == measure &
                   sdt_tbl$contrast == "language_difference" & sdt_tbl$session %in% ss, , drop = FALSE]
    r[match(ss, r$session), , drop = FALSE]
  }
  .cred <- function(r) !is.na(r$ci_low) & (r$ci_low > 0 | r$ci_high < 0)
  gs <- ld("gender_agreement", "sensitivity"); gc <- ld("gender_agreement", "criterion")
  avg <- .sdt_row("gender_agreement", "criterion", "language_difference", "average")
  last2 <- utils::tail(seq_along(ss), 2)
  fails <- c(
    if (any(.cred(gs) & gs$median > 0, na.rm = TRUE)) "the Mini-Norwegian group is credibly more sensitive to gender agreement at some session",
    if (!all(gs$median < 0, na.rm = TRUE)) "the Mini-Norwegian sensitivity estimate is no longer the lower at every session",
    if (any(unlist(lapply(c("differential_object_marking", "verb_object_number_agreement"),
                          function(p) .cred(ld(p, "sensitivity")))), na.rm = TRUE))
      "a control property now shows a credible sensitivity difference",
    if (isTRUE(.cred(gc[1, ]))) "the criterion difference is credible at Session 2",
    if (!all(.cred(gc[last2, ]) & gc$median[last2] < 0)) "the criterion difference is not credible, with the Mini-Norwegian group the more liberal, at both of the last two sessions",
    if (is.null(avg) || !(avg$ci_high < 0)) "the criterion difference averaged over sessions is not credibly negative")
  if (!length(fails)) return("")
  paste0(" **[Check: the abstract, Discussion and Conclusion state otherwise, but ",
         paste(fails, collapse = "; "), ".]**")
}
# The direction of the gender-agreement criterion difference at the last two sessions in
# every accuracy fit of that property (reported, refits and sensitivity analyses), as the
# lowest posterior probability that the Mini-Norwegian criterion was the more liberal, floored
# so that "at least" holds. A marker replaces it if any fit puts a difference the other way.
crit_direction_clause <- function() {
  if (is.null(sdt_tbl)) return("*[pending signal-detection summaries]*")
  last2 <- as.character(utils::tail(LES_ERP_SESSIONS, 2))
  r <- sdt_tbl[startsWith(sdt_tbl$model, "accuracy_gender_agreement") &
                 sdt_tbl$measure == "criterion" & sdt_tbl$contrast == "language_difference" &
                 sdt_tbl$session %in% last2, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(r)) return("*[signal-detection contrast not found]*")
  if (any(r$median >= 0)) {
    return(paste0("**[Check: in some fit the gender-agreement criterion difference at the last ",
                  "two sessions no longer has the Mini-Norwegian group as the more liberal. ",
                  "Revise this sentence.]**"))
  }
  # The sentence it completes has already said "in every fit", so this says "in each".
  sprintf(paste0("with a posterior probability of at least %s in each that the ",
                 "Mini-Norwegian criterion was the more liberal at Sessions %s and %s"),
          sub("^0", "", formatC(floor(100 * min(r$pd)) / 100, format = "f", digits = 2)),
          last2[1], last2[2])
}
# How far the refit with the by-participant grammaticality x session slope moved the
# gender-agreement criterion difference at any session, as the largest absolute change in
# its median, rounded up.
crit_maxranef_shift <- function() {
  ss <- as.character(LES_ERP_SESSIONS)
  d <- vapply(ss, function(s) {
    a <- .sdt_row("gender_agreement", "criterion", "language_difference", s)
    b <- .sdt_row("gender_agreement", "criterion", "language_difference", s,
                  model = "accuracy_gender_agreement_maxranef")
    if (is.null(a) || is.null(b)) NA_real_ else abs(a$median - b$median)
  }, numeric(1))
  if (anyNA(d)) return("*[signal-detection contrast pending]*")
  apa_num(ceiling(100 * max(d)) / 100, digits = 2)
}
# Typed claims about the refit with the by-participant grammaticality x session slope, made
# in the abstract, the Results, the Discussion, Strength of evidence and the Conclusion: with
# that slope the gender-agreement criterion difference is credible at no session and not
# averaged over sessions, its growth between Sessions 2 and 6 is credible in the reported
# fit but not in the refit, and at the last two sessions every fit has the Mini-Norwegian
# group as the more liberal. Each failure is named.
maxranef_claims_guard <- function() {
  mx <- "accuracy_gender_agreement_maxranef"
  if (is.null(sdt_tbl) || !.has_sdt_model(mx)) return("")
  .cred <- function(r) !is.null(r) && (r$ci_low > 0 || r$ci_high < 0)
  grow <- function(model) .sdt_row("gender_agreement", "criterion",
                                   "change_first_to_last_language_difference", "2->6", model = model)
  fails <- c(
    if (!identical(sdt_credible_sessions("gender_agreement", "criterion", model = mx), "no session"))
      "the criterion difference is credible at some session with the added slope",
    if (.cred(.sdt_row("gender_agreement", "criterion", "language_difference", "average", model = mx)))
      "the criterion difference averaged over sessions is credible with the added slope",
    if (!.cred(grow("accuracy_gender_agreement")) || .cred(grow(mx)))
      "the growth of the criterion difference is no longer credible only in the reported fit",
    if (startsWith(crit_direction_clause(), "*"))
      "some fit no longer has the Mini-Norwegian criterion as the more liberal at the last two sessions")
  if (!length(fails)) return("")
  paste0(" **[Check: the abstract, Results, Discussion and Conclusion grade the criterion ",
         "difference as suggestive because the refit with the added slope does not support it, but ",
         paste(fails, collapse = "; "), ".]**")
}
# The differential-object-marking contrast in the change of sensitivity between Sessions 3
# and 6, in the reported fit and the two refits with the added slope: whether each interval
# includes zero, so the sentence follows the estimates.
dom_edge_clause <- function() {
  ids <- paste0("accuracy_differential_object_marking", c("", "_maxranef", "_maxranef_byitem"))
  r <- lapply(ids, function(id) .sdt_row("differential_object_marking", "sensitivity",
                                         "change_first_to_last_language_difference", "3->6",
                                         model = id))
  if (any(vapply(r, is.null, logical(1)))) return("*[signal-detection contrast pending]*")
  cr <- vapply(r, function(x) x$ci_low > 0 || x$ci_high < 0, logical(1))
  .ex <- function(c) if (c) "excluded" else "included"
  .rep <- function(i) report_sdt("differential_object_marking", "sensitivity",
                                 "change_first_to_last_language_difference", "3->6", model = ids[i])
  if (all(cr == cr[1])) {
    sprintf(paste0("Its interval %s zero, as it did in the refit with the added slope (%s) and ",
                   "in the refit that adds the by-item term as well (%s)."), .ex(cr[1]), .rep(2), .rep(3))
  } else {
    sprintf(paste0("Its interval %s zero, and it %s zero in the refit with the added slope (%s) ",
                   "and %s zero in the refit that adds the by-item term as well (%s)."),
            .ex(cr[1]), .ex(cr[2]), .rep(2), .ex(cr[3]), .rep(3))
  }
}
# The Discussion's reference back to that contrast: the Mini-Norwegian group's decline is
# the smaller in the reported fit's estimate, and its interval includes zero there.
dom_sens_guard <- function() {
  r <- .sdt_row("differential_object_marking", "sensitivity",
                "change_first_to_last_language_difference", "3->6")
  if (is.null(r) || (r$median > 0 && r$ci_low <= 0)) return("")
  " **[Check: the differential-object-marking sensitivity contrast between Sessions 3 and 6 is now credible or runs the other way. Revise this sentence.]**"
}

# The item factor the judgement trials share with the ERP data: a sentence frame, identified
# by the trigger the presentation software sent with it (item_id = language x trigger),
```
