# counted by 02_extract_accuracy.R over the modelled trials. Until 3 October 2026 this
# clause described logged sentence texts, which are nested in grammaticality and recur
# across few participants; the frame is the unit that crosses grammaticality and session.
item_inv_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_accuracy_item_inventory.csv"))
item_inventory_clause <- function() {
  d <- item_inv_tbl
  if (is.null(d) || !nrow(d) || anyNA(d$n_items)) {
    return("*[item inventory pending the accuracy extraction]*")
  }
  d <- d[match(names(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_PROSE), d$grammatical_property), , drop = FALSE]
  d <- d[!is.na(d$grammatical_property), , drop = FALSE]
  every <- all(d$share_items_both_grammaticality == 1) && all(d$n_trials_without_item == 0)
  sprintf(paste0("each property has %s frames, half in each miniature language, and %s ",
                 "frame was judged under both grammaticality levels and by between %s and %s ",
                 "participants (medians %s for %s)"),
          if (length(unique(d$n_items)) == 1L) d$n_items[1] else paste(d$n_items, collapse = ", "),
          if (every) "every" else "nearly every",
          min(d$participants_per_item_min), max(d$participants_per_item_max),
          paste(paste(utils::head(d$participants_per_item_median, -1), collapse = ", "),
                utils::tail(d$participants_per_item_median, 1), sep = " and "),
          paste(paste(unname(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_PROSE[utils::head(d$grammatical_property, -1)]),
                      collapse = ", "),
                unname(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_PROSE[utils::tail(d$grammatical_property, 1)]),
                sep = " and "))
}

# The sample is described as bilinguals rather than adults because the youngest
# participant was under 18 at the time of the questionnaire. That is a fact about the
# participants, not a rounding artefact: exactly one LHQ3 record gives an age below 18
# (the next lowest is 18), and that person contributes trials to the fitted models. The
# sentence is emitted from the data, so it disappears by itself if the minimum ever rises
# to 18 or above. The ethics sentence of the Participants paragraph that names the
# 16-year-old participant is typed on purpose, to stay word for word what the ethics
# declaration says; only this demographic clause is emitted from the data.
minors_note <- function() {
  if (is.null(parts_tbl)) return("")
  r <- parts_tbl[parts_tbl$metric == "age_years", , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(r) != 1 || is.na(r$vmin) || r$vmin >= 18) return("")
  paste0(" The youngest participant was under 18 at the time of the questionnaire.",
         " All others were adults.")
}
# Canonical pooled ERP retention (mean / SD trials retained per modelled cell).
erp_ret <- function(field = "mean") {
  if (is.null(erp_ret_tbl) || !"scope" %in% names(erp_ret_tbl)) return("NN")
  r <- erp_ret_tbl[erp_ret_tbl$scope %in% "canonical", , drop = FALSE]
  cand <- intersect(c(field, paste0(field, "_retained")), names(r))
  if (nrow(r) < 1 || !length(cand)) return("NN")
  apa_num(mean(r[[cand[1]]], na.rm = TRUE), digits = 1)
}

# Figures of the September audit of the EEG exports (paper_1_transfer/audit/, ISSUES.md N6
# and N7), read from the long table make_audit_tables.py writes. aud() formats one quantity
# (abs = TRUE for a signed gap reported as a size); aud_ci() gives its 95% interval. Both
# print a marked fallback when the table or the quantity is absent.
.aud_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_audit_trial_loss.csv"))
.aud_row <- function(q) {
  if (is.null(.aud_tbl)) return(NULL)
  r <- .aud_tbl[.aud_tbl$quantity == q, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(r) == 1L && is.finite(r$value)) r else NULL
}
aud <- function(q, digits = 0, abs = FALSE) {
  r <- .aud_row(q)
  if (is.null(r)) return("*[audit figure pending]*")
  v <- if (abs) base::abs(r$value) else r$value
  if (digits == 0) formatC(round(v), format = "d", big.mark = ",") else apa_num(v, digits = digits)
}
aud_ci <- function(q, digits = 2) {
  r <- .aud_row(q)
  if (is.null(r) || !is.finite(r$ci_low)) return("*[audit interval pending]*")
  sprintf("95%% CI $[%s, %s]$", apa_num(r$ci_low, digits = digits), apa_num(r$ci_high, digits = digits))
}

# Rejection rate and the grammatical-vs-ungrammatical retention gap, from the
# per-condition rows. Reported so that differential trial loss between the compared
# conditions is shown to be absent rather than merely assumed.
.ret_pc <- function() {
  if (is.null(erp_ret_tbl) || !"scope" %in% names(erp_ret_tbl)) return(NULL)
  d <- erp_ret_tbl[erp_ret_tbl$scope %in% "per_condition_canonical", , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(d)) NULL else d
}
ret_by_gram <- function(level) {
  d <- .ret_pc()
  if (is.null(d) || !"grammaticality" %in% names(d)) return("NN")
  # Two decimals, as ret_gram_gap() prints the gap: at one, means 0.05 apart can print as
  # 31.5 and 31.4 beside "a difference of 0.05".
  apa_num(mean(d$mean_retained[d$grammaticality == level], na.rm = TRUE), digits = 2)
}
ret_gram_gap <- function() {
  d <- .ret_pc()
  if (is.null(d) || !"grammaticality" %in% names(d)) return("NN")
  g <- mean(d$mean_retained[d$grammaticality == "Grammatical"], na.rm = TRUE)
  u <- mean(d$mean_retained[d$grammaticality == "Ungrammatical"], na.rm = TRUE)
  apa_num(abs(g - u), digits = 2)
}

# --- Multivariate decoding follow-up (scripts 08/09) --------------------------
# The timecourse CSVs carry the cluster-permutation p AND the post-hoc
# within-property Benjamini-Hochberg FDR columns (cluster_p_fdr / significant_fdr);
# the generalisation CSVs hold descriptive cross-language AUC (no permutation null).
# Display labels for plots, from the data manifest (_shared/R/03_data_manifest.R), which
# is the single source of the property order for both manuscripts. Two conventions are
# deliberate.
# (1) ORDER. The properties are listed in the order they were introduced across
#     sessions -- gender agreement (Session 2), differential object marking
#     (Session 3), verb-object number agreement (Session 4) -- and every figure, table
#     and list in the manuscript follows that order. Alphabetical ordering would
#     scramble the design and is never used.
# (2) LITERAL CHARACTERS. These strings are rendered by the graphics device, not by
#     Pandoc, so a LaTeX-style "--" would appear verbatim in the figure. Body-text
#     prose uses the en-dash form (LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_PROSE) separately.
.decode_props <- LES_PROPERTY_LABELS
# The same labels for tables, which Pandoc typesets, so the en dash the running text
# uses can be written as "--".
.table_props <- LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_TABLE
decode_tc  <- setNames(lapply(names(.decode_props), function(p)
  .read_csv_if(paper1_results(paste0(p, "_decoding_timecourse.csv")))), names(.decode_props))
decode_gen <- setNames(lapply(names(.decode_props), function(p)
  .read_csv_if(paper1_results(paste0(p, "_decoding_generalization.csv")))), names(.decode_props))
decode_ready <- any(!vapply(decode_tc, is.null, logical(1)))

# Permutation count actually used, read back from the decoding artefacts, and the
# resulting floor on an attainable cluster p, 1/(B + 1) (the observed statistic counts
# as one draw from the null; Phipson & Smyth, 2010). Both were previously typed into the
# Methods as "200 shufflings" and ".005", which would silently misdescribe the analysis
# the moment the decoding is re-run at a different B -- as it is being, at B = 1000.
#
# The count is read PER INFERENCE STRATUM, because the two strata can legitimately differ
# while a rerun is in progress. The confirmatory family is the pooled overall time-course,
# so its blocks are the ones whose permutation count governs every cluster-level decision
# the manuscript reports, whereas the exploratory breakdowns enter no family and carry
# their own count. Splitting them lets the Method quote the count behind the reported
# decisions instead of collapsing to a range that describes neither stratum. The fallback,
# for an artefact written before the `inference` column existed, is the analysis label that
# column is derived from.
.n_perm_stratum <- function(confirmatory = TRUE) {
  v <- unlist(lapply(decode_tc, function(d) {
    if (is.null(d)) return(NULL)
    sel <- if ("inference" %in% names(d)) d$inference == "confirmatory"
           else d$analysis == "overall"
    d$n_perm[if (confirmatory) sel else !sel]
  }))
  v <- unique(v[is.finite(v)])
  if (!length(v)) NA_integer_ else v
}
.n_perm_conf <- function() .n_perm_stratum(TRUE)
.n_perm_expl <- function() .n_perm_stratum(FALSE)
# This is spliced into "The permutation null comprised <...> shufflings", so it must stay a
# bare count. Where the exploratory breakdowns lag the confirmatory family, that is
# disclosed by decode_expl_pending() in the following sentence rather than crammed in here.
n_perm_txt <- function() {
  v <- .n_perm_conf()
  if (all(is.na(v))) return("*[pending decoding run]*")
  # A confirmatory family still spanning several counts is a half-pulled rerun, and
  # collapsing it to one number would misdescribe the analysis.
  if (length(v) > 1) return(paste0(min(v), "--", max(v), " (mixed; re-run incomplete)"))
  formatC(v, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
}
# The exploratory counts that LAG the confirmatory one, formatted for prose. Empty when
# nothing lags, which is what retires the narrower disclosure.
.n_perm_expl_txt <- function() {
  b <- .n_perm_conf(); e <- .n_perm_expl()
  if (all(is.na(e)) || length(b) != 1L) return("")
  e <- sort(unique(e[is.finite(e) & e < b]))
  if (!length(e)) return("")
  paste(formatC(e, format = "d", big.mark = ","), collapse = " and ")
}
# WHICH properties lag, named for prose. Without this the disclosure reads as though every
# property's breakdowns were affected, when a rerun can leave one property behind and not
# the others. The prose form is used because .decode_props carries the literal hyphen
# the graphics device needs, not the en-dash body text uses.
.n_perm_expl_props <- function() {
  b <- .n_perm_conf()
  if (length(b) != 1L || is.na(b)) return("")
  lags <- vapply(names(.decode_props), function(p) {
    d <- decode_tc[[p]]
    if (is.null(d)) return(FALSE)
    sel <- if ("inference" %in% names(d)) d$inference != "confirmatory"
           else d$analysis != "overall"
    any(d$n_perm[sel] < b, na.rm = TRUE)
  }, logical(1))
  if (!any(lags)) return("")
  nm <- unname(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_PROSE[names(.decode_props)[lags]])
  if (length(nm) == 1L) return(nm)
  paste(paste(nm[-length(nm)], collapse = ", "), "and", nm[length(nm)])
}
# The permutation floor 1/(B + 1), stated as the exact fraction, so that it agrees with the
# "p < .001" that dec_min_p() prints for a cluster at the floor of a 1,000-shuffle null.
min_cluster_p <- function() {
  v <- .n_perm_conf()
  if (all(is.na(v)) || length(v) > 1) return("*[pending decoding run]*")
  paste0("1/", formatC(v + 1, format = "d", big.mark = ","))
}

# --- Status of the decoding cluster-level inference ---------------------------
# Two disclosures live here, and both are emitted from the artefacts rather than typed, so
# that neither can outlive the state it describes.
#
# The first, decode_provisional(), covers the state the artefacts were in until the
# confirmatory rerun landed: FDR columns written by an earlier revision of
# scripts/09_run_decoding.R, which corrected across ALL of a property's clusters (the pooled
# overall time-course together with the session-resolved and session-by-language
# breakdowns) rather than across the clusters of the pooled overall time-course alone, the
# family the Method describes and the family the current script implements. At B = 200 that
# script also refuses the confirmatory correction outright, because the attainable p-floor
# 1/(B + 1) exceeds the smallest Benjamini-Hochberg threshold the family admits. The notice
# retires itself once every property's CONFIRMATORY rows carry an `inference` column and the
# planned permutation count, which they now do.
#
# The second, decode_expl_pending(), is narrower and is what currently fires: the
# confirmatory family is settled, and only the exploratory breakdowns of the properties
# named by .n_perm_expl_props() still rest on the coarser null while their blocks finish.
# Because those breakdowns enter no correction family, they cannot move a confirmatory
# decision, so this notice qualifies the breakdowns and leaves the decisions standing.
# The permutation count the decoding job plans (hpc/08_decoding.slurm refuses fewer). Kept
# here and not in scripts/_config.R, which is part of the decoding tensor fingerprint.
.LES_P1_DECODE_NPERM_PLANNED <- 1000L
decode_provisional <- function() {
  if (!decode_ready) return(FALSE)
  # Every property's time-course present must carry the inference column, as the comment
  # above says; any() would retire the notice as soon as one property had it.
  tcs <- Filter(Negate(is.null), decode_tc)
  finalised <- length(tcs) > 0 &&
    all(vapply(tcs, function(d) "inference" %in% names(d), logical(1)))
  b <- .n_perm_conf()
  !finalised || all(is.na(b)) || any(b < .LES_P1_DECODE_NPERM_PLANNED)
}
# Whether the EXPLORATORY breakdowns still rest on a coarser null than the confirmatory
# time-courses. This is a strictly narrower disclosure than decode_provisional(): it leaves
# every reported cluster-level decision standing and qualifies only the breakdowns, which
# enter no correction family and so cannot move a confirmatory decision. It retires by
# itself once the outstanding blocks are pulled back at the confirmatory count.
decode_expl_pending <- function() {
  if (!decode_ready || decode_provisional()) return(FALSE)
  e <- .n_perm_expl(); b <- .n_perm_conf()
  !all(is.na(e)) && length(b) == 1L && any(e < b)
}
decode_status_method <- function() {
  if (!decode_provisional()) {
    # A property whose run is still completing its secondary analyses (see
    # .decode_run_done() below) has a final confirmatory time-course assembled from its
    # banked pooled block, and its secondary analyses still to come.
    if (decode_runs_pending()) return(paste0(
      " One qualification belongs with that description. Every confirmatory time-course ",
      "reported here rests on the full permutation null and is corrected under exactly the ",
      "family just defined. The decoding runs for ", .decode_runs_pending_txt(), " were ",
      "still completing their secondary analyses, so their confirmatory time-courses were ",
      "assembled from the banked pooled block by a script that checks every block against ",
      "the decoding data before using it, and their session-resolved breakdowns, ",
      "cross-language and temporal-generalisation analyses will be reported once those runs ",
      "finish. None of these analyses enters the correction family, so none can alter a ",
      "confirmatory decision."))
    if (!decode_expl_pending()) return("")
    return(paste0(
      " One qualification belongs with that description. The confirmatory time-courses ",
      "reported here were corrected under exactly the family just defined, and at the full ",
      "permutation null. The exploratory breakdowns for ", .n_perm_expl_props(), ", which ",
      "enter no family, are still those of an earlier run at ", .n_perm_expl_txt(),
      " shufflings, so their cluster-level $p$ values resolve less finely than the ",
      "confirmatory ones. A rerun that brings them to the same null is under way, and by ",
      "construction it cannot alter a confirmatory decision."))
  }
  paste0(
    " One disclosure belongs with that description. The false-discovery-rate columns in ",
    "the decoding artefacts reported here were written under a wider family than the one ",
    "just defined: correction there ran across all of a property's clusters, the ",
    "session-resolved breakdowns included, rather than across the clusters of its pooled ",
    "overall time-course alone. A rerun of the decoding under the family defined here, ",
    "with a permutation null of 1,000 shufflings, is in progress, and the cluster-level ",
    "decisions reported below are provisional pending it. Which clusters survive depends ",
    "on both the family and the resolution of the null, so those decisions are expected ",
    "to change, most of all where a cluster-level $p$ lies at the attainable floor.")
}
decode_status_appendix <- function() {
  if (!decode_provisional()) {
    if (decode_runs_pending()) return(paste0(
      " The confirmatory decisions reported here rest on the family just defined and on the ",
      "full permutation null. Only the secondary analyses of ", .decode_runs_pending_txt(),
      " are still running, and no decision in the confirmatory family depends on them."))
    if (!decode_expl_pending()) return("")
    return(paste0(
      " The confirmatory decisions reported here rest on the family just defined and on the ",
      "full permutation null. Only the exploratory breakdowns for ", .n_perm_expl_props(),
      " still carry the coarser null of the earlier run, and no decision in the confirmatory ",
      "family depends on them."))
  }
  paste0(
    " The wider family just argued against is nevertheless the one behind the ",
    "false-discovery-rate columns in the artefacts this draft reports, which predate the ",
    "current definition. That is why the cluster-level decoding decisions are labelled ",
    "provisional in the Method and the Results, and it is what the rerun described there ",
    "resolves.")
}
decode_status_transparency <- function() {
  if (!decode_provisional()) {
    if (decode_runs_pending()) return(paste0(
      " One analysis is not yet complete, and we flag it here as well as where it is ",
      "reported. The confirmatory decoding time-courses are final, but the secondary decoding ",
      "analyses for ", .decode_runs_pending_txt(), " are still running. Because those analyses ",
      "enter no correction family, their completion cannot alter a confirmatory decision."))
    if (!decode_expl_pending()) return("")
    return(paste0(
      " One analysis is not yet uniform, and we flag it here as well as where it is ",
      "reported. The confirmatory decoding time-courses are final: they are corrected under ",
      "the family the Method describes and rest on the full permutation null. The ",
      "session-resolved breakdowns for ", .n_perm_expl_props(), " are still those of an ",
      "earlier, coarser run, and a rerun that brings them to the same null is in progress. ",
      "Because those breakdowns enter no correction family, the rerun cannot alter a ",
      "confirmatory decision, in either direction."))
  }
  paste0(
    " One analysis is not yet final, and we flag it here as well as where it is ",
    "reported. The decoding cluster-level inference rests on artefacts whose ",
    "false-discovery-rate correction spanned a wider family than the Method describes, ",
    "and a rerun under the described family, with a larger permutation null, is in ",
    "progress. Until it lands, no cluster-level decoding decision should be read as ",
    "settled, in either direction.")
}
decode_status_results <- function() {
  if (!decode_provisional()) {
    if (decode_runs_pending()) return(paste0(
      " One qualification attaches to this section. The confirmatory cluster-level decisions ",
      "are final. The secondary analyses for ", .decode_runs_pending_txt(), " are still ",
      "running, so their cross-language peaks below are marked as pending."))
    if (!decode_expl_pending()) return("")
    return(paste0(
      " One qualification attaches to this section. The confirmatory cluster-level decisions ",
      "are final. The session-resolved breakdowns for ", .n_perm_expl_props(), " still rest ",
      "on the earlier, coarser permutation null, so their cluster-level $p$ values resolve ",
      "less finely, and the rerun that will bring them to the same null is still running."))
  }
  paste0(
    " The cluster-level decisions in this section are provisional. As set out under ",
    "*Multivariate decoding* in the Method, the correction family behind the ",
    "false-discovery-rate columns in the present artefacts is wider than the one described ",
    "there, and the permutation null behind them is coarse enough that several ",
    "cluster-level $p$ values sit at the smallest value it can attain. The rerun under the ",
    "confirmatory family will settle which clusters survive. We therefore report the counts ",
    "as the artefacts hold them and draw no conclusion from a property's having none.")
}

# Cross-property generalisation (train on one property's contrast, test on another):
# one CSV per training property, pooled here. Descriptive AUC, no permutation null.
decode_xprop <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), lapply(names(.decode_props), function(p)
  .read_csv_if(paper1_results(paste0(p, "_decoding_generalization_crossproperty.csv"))))))
# Peak AUC over all train->test property pairs (NA-safe; "NN" if the stage has not run).
# Restricted to the post-stimulus axis (time_ms >= 0): the maximum of a noisy,
# autocorrelated pre-stimulus AUC time-course carries no information about a violation
# response and would only inflate an apparent effect (see the pre-stimulus control below).
xprop_max <- function(digits = 2) {
  if (is.null(decode_xprop) || !nrow(decode_xprop)) return("NN")
  x <- if ("time_ms" %in% names(decode_xprop)) decode_xprop[decode_xprop$time_ms >= 0, ] else decode_xprop
  apa_num(max(x$auc, na.rm = TRUE), digits = digits)
}
# The train-test pair at that peak, for prose ("gender agreement was tested on differential
# object marking"), so that the direction named beside the peak is read from the artefact.
xprop_max_pair <- function() {
  if (is.null(decode_xprop) || !nrow(decode_xprop) ||
      !all(c("train_set", "test_set") %in% names(decode_xprop))) return("*[pending decoding run]*")
  x <- if ("time_ms" %in% names(decode_xprop)) decode_xprop[decode_xprop$time_ms >= 0, ] else decode_xprop
  i <- which.max(x$auc)
  sprintf("%s was tested on %s", LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_PROSE[[x$train_set[i]]],
          LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_PROSE[[x$test_set[i]]])
}

# Per-property decoding summary. Peak AUC and its latency are reported on the
# POST-STIMULUS axis only (time_ms >= 0), because a grammaticality decoder that peaks
# before the critical word is decoding a confound, not a violation response. The
# pre-stimulus interval is retained separately as an explicit negative control
# (mean/peak AUC and the count of FDR-significant pre-stimulus samples), which is
# itself a key diagnostic and is reported in the text. FDR-significant cluster counts
# (whole family and the primary overall time-course) span the full epoch so that any
# pre-stimulus cluster is disclosed rather than hidden.
decode_summary <- function(prop) {
  d <- decode_tc[[prop]]; if (is.null(d)) return(NULL)
  has_fdr <- "cluster_p_fdr" %in% names(d)
  cols <- c("analysis", "level", "cluster_id", "cluster_p", if (has_fdr) "cluster_p_fdr")
  cl   <- unique(d[!is.na(d$cluster_id), cols, drop = FALSE])
  ov   <- d[d$analysis == "overall", ]
  post <- ov[ov$time_ms >= 0, ]
  pre  <- ov[ov$time_ms <  0, ]
  peak_i <- if (nrow(post)) which.max(post$auc) else NA_integer_
  g    <- decode_gen[[prop]]
  # The confirmatory rows are the pooled overall time-course; an artefact written before
  # the `inference` column existed marks them by analysis == "overall".
  conf <- if ("inference" %in% names(d)) d$inference %in% "confirmatory" else d$analysis == "overall"
  clo  <- unique(d[conf & !is.na(d$cluster_id), c("cluster_id", "cluster_p"), drop = FALSE])
  cqo  <- if (has_fdr) unique(d[conf & !is.na(d$cluster_id), c("cluster_id", "cluster_p_fdr"),
                                drop = FALSE]) else NULL
  list(n_fdr         = if (has_fdr) sum(cl$cluster_p_fdr < .05, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_integer_,
       n_overall_fdr = if (has_fdr) sum(cl$cluster_p_fdr < .05 & cl$analysis == "overall", na.rm = TRUE) else NA_integer_,
       # The confirmatory clusters, those that pass the maximum-cluster test on its own (the
       # first of the two correction layers), and the smallest value the second layer leaves.
       # Without them a property whose clusters the second layer removes would read as a
       # plain null, although the first layer already controls the family-wise error rate
       # across time (see the appendix on the decoding correction family).
       n_overall_conf = nrow(clo),
       n_overall_fwer = sum(clo$cluster_p < .05, na.rm = TRUE),
       min_q_overall  = if (!is.null(cqo) && nrow(cqo))
         suppressWarnings(min(cqo$cluster_p_fdr, na.rm = TRUE)) else NA_real_,
       min_clp       = if (nrow(cl)) suppressWarnings(min(cl$cluster_p, na.rm = TRUE)) else NA_real_,
       min_clp_overall = if (nrow(clo)) suppressWarnings(min(clo$cluster_p, na.rm = TRUE)) else NA_real_,
       max_auc_ov    = if (nrow(post)) max(post$auc, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
       peak_ms       = if (!is.na(peak_i)) post$time_ms[peak_i] else NA_real_,
       pre_mean_auc  = if (nrow(pre)) mean(pre$auc, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
       pre_max_auc   = if (nrow(pre)) max(pre$auc, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
       pre_n_fdr     = if (has_fdr && nrow(pre)) sum(pre$significant_fdr %in% c(TRUE, "TRUE"), na.rm = TRUE) else NA_integer_,
       # Post-stimulus only, for the reason given above: a cross-language AUC peaking
       # before the critical word is not a violation response.
       max_auc_xlang = if (!is.null(g)) {
         gp <- if ("time_ms" %in% names(g)) g[g$time_ms >= 0, , drop = FALSE] else g
         if (nrow(gp)) max(gp$auc, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_
       } else NA_real_)
}
dec_gender <- decode_summary("gender_agreement")
dec_dom    <- decode_summary("differential_object_marking")
dec_verb   <- decode_summary("verb_object_number_agreement")

# Whether a property's full decoding run has finished. Step 09 runs the time-course, then
# the cross-language generalisation, then the temporal generalisation, and writes each CSV
# when its stage ends, so a finished run leaves both generalisation files, whereas a
# time-course assembled early from the banked confirmatory block
# (scripts/09b_assemble_confirmatory_timecourse.R) comes without them. Requiring the
# temporal-generalisation file as well keeps a run stopped by its wall during that last
# stage from passing for finished. The generalisation files carry no record of the sample
# they were computed on, which is why those of the earlier, uncorrected sample were removed
# from results/ on 10 October 2026 instead of being left beside time-courses from the
# corrected one.
.decode_run_done <- function(p) !is.null(decode_tc[[p]]) && !is.null(decode_gen[[p]]) &&
  file.exists(paper1_results(paste0(p, "_decoding_temporal_generalization.csv")))
.decode_runs_pending_props <- function() {
  names(.decode_props)[vapply(names(.decode_props), function(p)
    !is.null(decode_tc[[p]]) && !.decode_run_done(p), logical(1))]
}
decode_runs_pending <- function() decode_ready && !decode_provisional() &&
  length(.decode_runs_pending_props()) > 0
# The description of differential object marking's temporal-generalisation matrix, computed
# from the matrix. Its conditions differ in the word before the critical word (the violation
# omits *fi*), and the decoder's input is baseline-subtracted (step 08), so the description
# is organised around what those two facts predict. Four values, each a mean AUC over fixed,
# descriptive windows on the matrix's 8 ms grid: decoders trained in the first third of the
# 100 ms baseline (-98 to -66 ms) tested on its last third (-34 to -2 ms); decoders trained
# in that last third tested on the first 100 ms after onset; decoders trained from 200 ms to
# the end of the epoch tested on the other latencies of that span (off the diagonal); and
# decoders trained in the last third of the baseline tested from 200 ms on. Subtracting a
# trial's baseline mean makes the conditions' difference average to zero over the baseline,
# so a difference that changes across it reverses sign there, which an AUC below 0.5 in the
# first value records. The words follow the numbers: a marker replaces the sentences when the
# first value is no longer below 0.48, the second no longer above 0.51, the third no longer
# above 0.52, or the fourth more than 0.02 from 0.50. No null was computed for the matrix, so
# the sentences only describe, and they say what the matrix cannot decide. "" while the
# matrix is absent.
dec_tgm_sentence <- function(prop) {
  m <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results(paste0(prop, "_decoding_temporal_generalization.csv")))
  if (is.null(m)) return("")
  chk <- paste0(" **[Check: the temporal-generalisation matrix no longer fits the sentences ",
                "that describe it. Revise them.]**")
  if (!all(c("train_time_ms", "test_time_ms", "auc") %in% names(m))) return(chk)
  tr <- m$train_time_ms; te <- m$test_time_ms
  first_bl <- function(x) x > -100 & x < -65
  last_bl  <- function(x) x > -35 & x < 0
  v <- c(rev   = mean(m$auc[first_bl(tr) & last_bl(te)]),
         carry = mean(m$auc[last_bl(tr) & te > 0 & te <= 100]),
         late  = mean(m$auc[tr >= 200 & te >= 200 & tr != te]),
         cross = mean(m$auc[last_bl(tr) & te >= 200]))
  ok <- all(is.finite(v)) && v[["rev"]] < 0.48 && v[["carry"]] > 0.51 &&
    v[["late"]] > 0.52 && abs(v[["cross"]] - 0.5) <= 0.02
  if (!ok) return(chk)
  sprintf(paste0(
    " The temporal-generalisation matrix shows how this separability is organised in time. ",
    "Decoders trained in the first third of the baseline classified its last third at a mean ",
    "AUC of %s, below chance, so the pattern separating the conditions reversed within the ",
    "baseline. Each trial's baseline mean is subtracted from the decoder's input, which makes ",
    "the conditions' difference average to zero over that interval, so a difference that ",
    "changes across it must reverse there. Decoders trained in the last third of the baseline ",
    "classified the first 100 ms after onset at %s, so that pattern carried across onset. From ",
    "200 ms to the end of the epoch a different pattern held. Decoders trained there classified ",
    "the other latencies of that span at %s, whereas those trained in the last third of the ",
    "baseline classified it at %s. The response to the differing preceding word ",
    "overlaps the epoch, and the subtraction carries the conditions' difference in the baseline ",
    "mean into every later sample, so the matrix cannot attribute that later pattern to a ",
    "violation response. No null distribution was computed for the matrix, so these values are ",
    "descriptive."),
    apa_num(v[["rev"]], digits = 2), apa_num(v[["carry"]], digits = 2),
    apa_num(v[["late"]], digits = 2), apa_num(v[["cross"]], digits = 2))
}
# The properties whose runs are still finishing, named for prose.
.decode_runs_pending_txt <- function() {
  nm <- unname(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_PROSE[.decode_runs_pending_props()])
  if (length(nm) <= 1L) return(paste(nm, collapse = ""))
  paste(paste(nm[-length(nm)], collapse = ", "), "and", nm[length(nm)])
}
# Counts below ten spelled out, as APA 7 asks of counts in running text.
.dec_num_word <- function(n) {
  if (length(n) != 1L || is.na(n)) return("NN")
  if (n >= 0 && n <= 9) c("no", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven",
                          "eight", "nine")[n + 1L] else format(n, big.mark = ",")
}
# A list of extents for prose, the last joined with "and".
.dec_and <- function(x) if (length(x) > 1L) paste(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = ", "), "and",
                                                  x[length(x)]) else paste(x, collapse = "")
# A time in milliseconds for prose. A negative time goes in math mode, as the typed prose
# writes one ("$-96$ to 1,096 ms"), so that it prints with a minus sign and not a hyphen.
.dec_ms <- function(x) { x <- round(x); if (x < 0) sprintf("$%s$", x) else as.character(x) }
# The cluster-level p values of a property's confirmatory clusters that pass the
# maximum-cluster test, formatted as one value or a range.
.dec_fwer_p_txt <- function(prop, survivors = NA) {
  d <- decode_tc[[prop]]
  keep <- d$analysis == "overall" & !is.na(d$cluster_id) & !is.na(d$cluster_p) & d$cluster_p < .05
  if (!is.na(survivors) && "cluster_p_fdr" %in% names(d))
    keep <- keep & ((d$cluster_p_fdr < .05) %in% survivors)
  pc <- unique(d[keep, c("cluster_id", "cluster_p"), drop = FALSE])$cluster_p
  if (!length(pc)) return("")
  one <- function(v) if (v < .001) "$p < .001$" else sprintf("$p = %s$", .dec_p3(v))
  if (length(unique(pc)) == 1L) one(pc[1]) else
    sprintf("$p$ from %s to %s", .dec_p3(min(pc)), .dec_p3(max(pc)))
}
# A p or q value for prose, as dec_min_p() prints one: leading zero dropped, three decimals.
.dec_p3 <- function(v) if (v < .001) "< .001" else sub("^0", "", formatC(v, format = "f", digits = 3))

# Extents of the confirmatory clusters that pass the maximum-cluster test on its own,
# whether or not they survive the second layer, in temporal order.
dec_fwer_spans <- function(prop) {
  d <- decode_tc[[prop]]
  if (is.null(d)) return(character(0))
  ov <- d[d$analysis == "overall" & !is.na(d$cluster_id) & !is.na(d$cluster_p) &
            d$cluster_p < .05, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(ov)) return(character(0))
  sp <- lapply(split(ov$time_ms, ov$cluster_id), range)
  sp <- sp[order(vapply(sp, `[`, 0, 1))]
  vapply(sp, function(x) sprintf("%s to %s ms", .dec_ms(x[1]), .dec_ms(x[2])), "")
}

# What the two correction layers left of a property's pooled time-course, as the sentence
# that follows its count of surviving clusters. The wording depends on the counts, so it is
# computed: surviving clusters are given with their extents; clusters that pass the
# maximum-cluster test but not the second layer are given with their extents, their
# cluster-level p values and the smallest adjusted value; and a time-course with neither
# says so with its smallest cluster-level p.
dec_layers_sentence <- function(s, prop) {
  if (is.null(s) || is.na(s$n_overall_fdr) || is.na(s$n_overall_fwer))
    return(" *[pending decoding run]*")
  if (s$n_overall_conf == 0L)
    return(" No sample of its time-course exceeded the cluster-forming threshold.")
  if (s$n_overall_fdr > 0) {
    out <- sprintf(" %s %s.", if (s$n_overall_fdr == 1L) "It spans" else "They span",
                   .dec_and(dec_fdr_spans(prop)))
    # The Method promises the clusters that pass the first test alongside the survivors, so
    # any that the second layer removed are named here too.
    extra <- s$n_overall_fwer - s$n_overall_fdr
    if (extra > 0) {
      fw <- setdiff(dec_fwer_spans(prop), dec_fdr_spans(prop))
      out <- paste0(out, sprintf(
        " A further %s passed the maximum-cluster test but not the second layer (%s, with cluster-level %s).",
        if (extra == 1L) "cluster" else paste(.dec_num_word(extra), "clusters"),
        .dec_and(fw), .dec_fwer_p_txt(prop, survivors = FALSE)))
    }
    return(out)
  }
  if (s$n_overall_fwer > 0) {
    return(sprintf(paste0(
      " Of its %s clusters, %s passed the maximum-cluster test on its own (%s, with ",
      "cluster-level %s), but the second layer removed %s, the smallest adjusted value being ",
      "$q = %s$."),
      .dec_num_word(s$n_overall_conf), .dec_num_word(s$n_overall_fwer),
      .dec_and(dec_fwer_spans(prop)), .dec_fwer_p_txt(prop),
      if (s$n_overall_fwer == 1L) "it" else "them all", .dec_p3(s$min_q_overall)))
  }
  if (s$n_overall_conf == 1L)
    return(sprintf(" Its one cluster did not pass the maximum-cluster test either (cluster-level %s).",
                   dec_min_p(s, "min_clp_overall")))
  sprintf(" None of its %s clusters passed the maximum-cluster test either (smallest cluster-level %s).",
          .dec_num_word(s$n_overall_conf), dec_min_p(s, "min_clp_overall"))
}
# How the size of the confirmatory family moves gender agreement's smallest p, for the
# appendix's disclosure. Benjamini-Hochberg gives the cluster with the smallest p the
# smallest of m * p(j) / j over the ordered p values, so the more clusters a time-course
# holds, the larger that adjusted value, short clusters included.
dec_m_sentence <- function(s = dec_gender) {
  # Only in the state the appendix sentence describes: clusters that pass the first layer
  # and none that survives the second, where the adjusted value is what decides.
  if (is.null(s) || is.na(s$min_q_overall) || is.na(s$min_clp_overall) ||
      .dec_gender_state() != "first") return("")
  pv <- if (s$min_clp_overall < .001) "$p < .001$" else sprintf("$p = %s$", .dec_p3(s$min_clp_overall))
  sprintf(" With its %s confirmatory clusters, the smallest cluster-level %s becomes $q = %s$.",
          .dec_num_word(s$n_overall_conf), pv, .dec_p3(s$min_q_overall))
}

# Guard on "Its pre-stimulus baseline sat at chance": silent while no confirmatory cluster
# that passes the maximum-cluster test reaches into the interval before the critical word.
dec_prestim_guard <- function(prop) {
  d <- decode_tc[[prop]]
  if (is.null(d)) return("")
  bad <- d$analysis == "overall" & !is.na(d$cluster_id) & d$cluster_p < .05 & d$time_ms < 0
  if (!any(bad, na.rm = TRUE)) return("")
  " **[Check: a cluster that passes the maximum-cluster test now reaches into the pre-stimulus interval. Revise this sentence.]**"
}

# The robustness analysis of the decoding, which leaves out the reprocessed and recovered
# records (LES_P1_EXCLUDE_REPROCESSED=1, files tagged "_exclreproc"). Its confirmatory
# counts are set beside the primary ones, and whether every property keeps its decision under
# both layers is computed, so the sentence cannot claim stability the files do not show.
decode_tc_rob <- setNames(lapply(names(.decode_props), function(p)
  .read_csv_if(paper1_results(paste0(p, "_exclreproc_decoding_timecourse.csv")))), names(.decode_props))
.dec_rob_counts <- function(d) {
  if (is.null(d) || !"cluster_p_fdr" %in% names(d)) return(NULL)
  conf <- if ("inference" %in% names(d)) d$inference %in% "confirmatory" else d$analysis == "overall"
  cl <- unique(d[conf & !is.na(d$cluster_id), c("cluster_id", "cluster_p", "cluster_p_fdr"), drop = FALSE])
  c(fdr = sum(cl$cluster_p_fdr < .05, na.rm = TRUE), fwer = sum(cl$cluster_p < .05, na.rm = TRUE))
}
dec_robust_sentence <- function() {
  rob <- lapply(decode_tc_rob, .dec_rob_counts)
  pri <- list(gender_agreement = dec_gender, differential_object_marking = dec_dom,
              verb_object_number_agreement = dec_verb)
  if (any(vapply(rob, is.null, logical(1))) || any(vapply(pri, is.null, logical(1))))
    return(" *[The robustness analysis of the decoding will be reported here once all three properties have run.]*")
  # The confirmatory decisions are those of both layers, so "the same" compares the counts
  # surviving both; the counts passing the first test are printed for both analyses, so a
  # change there is visible even when the decisions hold.
  same <- all(vapply(names(rob), function(p)
    isTRUE(rob[[p]][["fdr"]] == pri[[p]]$n_overall_fdr), logical(1)))
  w <- function(n) if (isTRUE(n == 0)) "zero" else .dec_num_word(n)
  lst <- function(v) paste0(v[1], ", ", v[2], " and ", v[3])
  rob_fdr  <- vapply(names(rob), function(p) w(rob[[p]][["fdr"]]), "")
  rob_fwer <- vapply(names(rob), function(p) w(rob[[p]][["fwer"]]), "")
  pri_fwer <- vapply(names(pri), function(p) w(pri[[p]]$n_overall_fwer), "")
  props <- unname(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_PROSE[names(rob)])
  sprintf(paste0(
    " In the robustness analysis, which leaves out the reprocessed and recovered records, %s. ",
    "The numbers of clusters surviving both layers were %s for %s, %s and %s, and the ",
    "numbers passing the maximum-cluster test, whether or not they survived the second layer, ",
    "were %s (%s in the primary analysis)."),
    if (same) "the confirmatory decisions were the same" else
      "the confirmatory decisions changed **[Check: revise the prose that relies on them]**",
    lst(rob_fdr), props[1], props[2], props[3], lst(rob_fwer), lst(pri_fwer))
}

# Guard on the typed parts of the sentences that say what the second layer did to gender
# agreement (the appendix on the correction family, the Discussion's grading of the
# decoding evidence). They hold while gender agreement has at least one cluster passing the
# maximum-cluster test and none surviving both layers, and a marker replaces silence
# otherwise.
dec_appx_guard <- function() {
  s <- dec_gender
  if (is.null(s) || is.na(s$n_overall_fdr) || is.na(s$n_overall_fwer))
    return(" *[pending decoding run]*")
  if (s$n_overall_fwer > 0 && s$n_overall_fdr == 0) return("")
  " **[Check: the second layer no longer separates gender agreement's clusters as this sentence states. Revise it.]**"
}

# The Discussion's three statements about gender agreement's separability. Each is worded
# from the two layers' counts, because the verdict changed once already between the run on
# the earlier sample (six clusters surviving both layers) and the run on the corrected one
# (none surviving both, four passing the maximum-cluster test), and typed wording would
# outlive the next change.
.dec_gender_state <- function() {
  s <- dec_gender
  if (is.null(s) || is.na(s$n_overall_fdr) || is.na(s$n_overall_fwer)) return("pending")
  if (s$n_overall_fdr > 0) "both" else if (s$n_overall_fwer > 0) "first" else "none"
}
dec_gender_sep_phrase <- function() {
  switch(.dec_gender_state(),
    pending = "*[pending decoding run]*",
    both    = "reliable pattern separability",
    first   = paste0("pattern separability that passed the maximum-cluster test but not the ",
                     "second correction layer, which we grade as suggestive"),
    none    = "no detectable pattern separability")
}
dec_gender_profile_sentence <- function() {
  switch(.dec_gender_state(),
    pending = "",
    both    = paste0(" That profile does not describe gender agreement here, which separates ",
                     "reliably as well as shifting the mean."),
    first   = paste0(" That profile may describe gender agreement in part, since its credible ",
                     "amplitude effect came with separability that passed the maximum-cluster ",
                     "test but not the second correction layer."),
    none    = paste0(" That profile fits gender agreement here, whose credible amplitude effect ",
                     "came with no detectable separability."))
}
dec_gender_grade_sentence <- function() {
  s <- dec_gender
  rob <- .dec_rob_counts(decode_tc_rob[["gender_agreement"]])
  switch(.dec_gender_state(),
    pending = " *[pending decoding run]*",
    both    = sprintf(paste0(" Gender agreement's %s surviving the confirmatory correction %s ",
                             "on the full permutation null and on a pre-stimulus baseline at chance%s."),
                      dec_count(s, "n_overall_fdr", "cluster"),
                      if (isTRUE(s$n_overall_fdr == 1L)) "rests" else "rest",
                      dec_prestim_guard("gender_agreement")),
    first   = sprintf(paste0(
      " Gender agreement has no cluster surviving the confirmatory correction, although %s%s ",
      "passed the maximum-cluster test, which by itself controls the family-wise error rate ",
      "across time. Its pre-stimulus baseline sat at chance%s, and we grade its separability ",
      "as suggestive."),
      dec_count(s, "n_overall_fwer", "cluster"),
      if (is.null(rob)) "" else sprintf(", and %s in the robustness analysis,",
        if (rob[["fwer"]] == 0) "none" else .dec_num_word(rob[["fwer"]])),
      dec_prestim_guard("gender_agreement")),
    none    = paste0(" Gender agreement has no cluster passing either correction layer, and we ",
                     "do not read its time-course as separable."))
}

# Inline accessor with a render-anytime placeholder for a not-yet-run decoding.
dec_val <- function(s, field, digits = NA) {
  if (is.null(s) || is.null(s[[field]]) || is.na(s[[field]])) return("*[pending decoding run]*")
  if (!is.na(digits)) apa_num(s[[field]], digits = digits) else as.character(s[[field]])
}
# A count and its noun, agreeing in number and spelled out below ten as APA prefers for
# small counts in prose. The alternative, an injected integer beside a typed "cluster(s)",
# leaves a programmer's hedge in the finished sentence.
dec_count <- function(s, field, noun) {
  if (is.null(s) || is.null(s[[field]]) || is.na(s[[field]]))
    return(paste0("*[pending decoding run]* ", noun, "s"))
  n <- as.integer(s[[field]])
  w <- if (n <= 9L) c("no", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven",
                      "eight", "nine")[n + 1L] else as.character(n)
  paste0(w, " ", noun, if (n == 1L) "" else "s")
}

# Largest absolute informative-vs-weak median shift among terms matching `pattern`,
# WITHIN one model family. The families sit on different scales: the ERP response is
# z-scored within participant, whereas the accuracy models are Bernoulli with a logit
# link and their coefficients are log-odds. A single maximum taken across both would be
# a scale-mixed quantity, and describing it as being "on the standardised scale" would
# misreport it -- here it would also inflate the ERP figure roughly seventyfold.
# Rows of the sensitivity table belonging to the primary structure. The table carries
# one comparison per structure, so an unfiltered maximum would report whichever
# structure happened to shift more, not the one the paper reports. Accuracy models have
# only one structure and are always kept.
.sens_primary <- function(tbl) {
  if (!"structure" %in% names(tbl)) {
    # A table written before the structure column existed can only describe the base
    # fits. Reporting its shift while the paper reports the maximal structure would be
    # the same silent mismatch as comparing across two samples, so return nothing and
    # let the caller print its pending marker.
    return(rep(identical(LES_P1_PRIMARY, "base"), nrow(tbl)))
  }
  # The reprocessed-excluded, diversity-covariate and reaction-time-screen refits are
  # sensitivity analyses on other data, so their shifts never enter the reported largest shift.
  (!grepl("^erp_", tbl$model) | tbl$structure %in% LES_P1_PRIMARY) &
    !grepl("_exclreproc|_diversity|_rtscreen|_nortscreen", tbl$model)
}

# The retention-free refits have no weak-prior counterpart unless one has been pooled;
# the qualification retires itself once _prior_sensitivity.csv carries a retfree row.
retfree_weak_note <- function(tbl = sens_tbl) {
  if (!is.null(tbl) && any(grepl("_retfree", tbl$model))) return("")
  " The retention-free refits were fitted under the informative priors only."
}

prior_shift_max <- function(pattern = "grammaticality", family = "^erp_", tbl = sens_tbl) {
  if (is.null(tbl)) return("*[pending sensitivity run]*")
  key <- grepl(pattern, tbl$parameter) & grepl(family, tbl$model) & .sens_primary(tbl)
  if (!any(key)) return("*[pending sensitivity run]*")
  v <- max(abs(tbl$median_shift[key]), na.rm = TRUE)
  # The sentence exists to show the shift is negligible, so keep enough decimals for
  # a negligible value to be legible rather than rounding it to a bare 0.00.
  apa_num(v, digits = if (v < 0.001) 4L else if (v < 0.1) 3L else 2L)
}

# Largest percentage difference between the informative and weak credible-interval
# widths, so the "widths unchanged" claim carries a measured bound rather than an
# assertion.
prior_width_dev <- function(pattern = "grammaticality", family = "^erp_", tbl = sens_tbl) {
  if (is.null(tbl)) return("*[pending sensitivity run]*")
  key <- grepl(pattern, tbl$parameter) & grepl(family, tbl$model) & .sens_primary(tbl) &
         is.finite(tbl$ci_width_weak) & tbl$ci_width_weak > 0
  if (!any(key)) return("*[pending sensitivity run]*")
  r <- tbl$ci_width_inf[key] / tbl$ci_width_weak[key]
  apa_num(100 * max(abs(r - 1)), digits = 1)
}

# --- Human-readable labels for the standardised model terms ------------------
.pretty_term <- function(x) {
  x |>
    gsub("^b_", "", x = _) |>
    gsub("z_recoded_grammaticality", "Grammaticality", x = _) |>
    gsub("z_recoded_session", "Session", x = _) |>
    gsub("z_recoded_mini_language", "Language", x = _) |>
    gsub("z_baseline_predictor", "Baseline", x = _) |>
    gsub("z_multilingual_language_diversity", "L1 dominance", x = _) |>
    gsub(":", " × ", x = _)   # multiplication sign, as in "Grammaticality × Session"
}

# --- Decimal precision that keeps a credible interval visibly clear of zero ---
# The ERP coefficients are small on the within-participant standardised scale
# (|b| is typically .005-.03), so a fixed two decimals prints an interval that
# genuinely excludes zero as e.g. [-0.02, 0.00] -- typographically identical to one
# that includes it, and so actively misleading about the inference. Widen to as many
# decimals as it takes for the bound nearest zero to show a non-zero digit, capped at
# four. Larger effects are unaffected and still print at two decimals, so precision
# tracks the magnitude being reported rather than being uniform and uninformative.
.les_digits <- function(med, lo, hi,
                        min_d = if (max(abs(c(med, lo, hi)), na.rm = TRUE) < 0.1) 3L else 2L,
                        max_d = 4L) {
  # The rule is simply that no non-zero quantity may print as zero. That matters most
  # for a credible interval, where a "0.00" bound contradicts the credibility claimed
  # for it in the text, but it applies equally to a median, which would otherwise
  # appear as the signed zero "-0.00". The floor is two decimals on the log-odds scale
  # of the accuracy models and three on the within-participant SD scale of the ERP
  # models, whose quantities are an order of magnitude smaller, so a median never prints
  # equal to its own bound; four decimals is the ceiling.
  v <- abs(c(med, lo, hi))
  v <- v[is.finite(v) & v > 0]
  if (!length(v)) return(min_d)
  d <- min_d
  while (d < max_d && round(min(v), d) == 0) d <- d + 1L
  d
}

# Vectorised formatter for the posterior-summary tables. Precision is the .les_digits
# rule applied to every row and the largest result used for the whole table (or for each
# level of `group`, for a table that mixes model families on different scales), so that
# decimals are uniform down a column, right alignment is decimal alignment, and a rounded
# bound can be told from a median. Negatives take the true minus sign (U+2212), which is
# also not a break point in LaTeX, so a value is never split as "-" / "0.002". The
# credible interval comes back as its two limits, `lo` and `hi`, which the tables print
# as the LL and UL columns. A missing value prints as an em dash, the tables' mark for a
# quantity expected but not available.
.fmt_est <- function(med, lo, hi, group = rep(TRUE, length(med))) {
  d <- integer(length(med))
  for (g in unique(group)) {
    k <- which(group == g)
    d[k] <- max(mapply(.les_digits, med[k], lo[k], hi[k]))
  }
  ff <- function(x) vapply(seq_along(x), function(i)
    if (is.finite(x[i])) les_minus(formatC(x[i], format = "f", digits = d[i])) else "—", "")
  list(median = ff(med), lo = ff(lo), hi = ff(hi))
}

# --- One pd format for the whole manuscript -----------------------------------
# .fmt_pd() and .pd_math() are defined in _shared/R/06_manuscript_helpers.R, which Paper 2
# sources as well, so that the companion papers print the probability of direction alike.

# --- Inline reporter: "b = m, 95% CrI [lo, hi], pd = .pp" ---------------------
# `exact = TRUE` reports the fit the id names, without routing it to the primary
# structure, which is how a base-structure fit (whose id is the bare cell id) is cited.
report_effect <- function(model_id, term, tbl = post_tbl, exact = FALSE) {
  if (is.null(tbl)) return("*[pending model fit]*")
  if (!exact) model_id <- .mid(model_id)   # resolve to the primary structure
  row <- tbl[tbl$model == model_id & tbl$parameter == term, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(row) != 1) return("*[term not found]*")
  d <- .les_digits(row$median, row$ci_low, row$ci_high)
  sprintf("$b = %s$, 95%% CrI $[%s, %s]$, $%s$",
          apa_num(row$median, digits = d), apa_num(row$ci_low, digits = d),
          apa_num(row$ci_high, digits = d), .pd_math(row$pd))
}

# Range of the probability of direction for one term across a set of ERP cells,
# e.g. "between .52 and .87". `model_pattern` is a regular expression selecting the
# cells, so it can pick a property, a window, or both. Injected rather than
# transcribed: both ranges in this manuscript were originally typed by hand, and one
# had silently gone stale by the time the models were refitted -- exactly the drift
# the render-anytime design exists to prevent.
pd_range <- function(term, model_pattern = "^erp_", sep = "and", tbl = post_tbl) {
  if (is.null(tbl)) return("*[pending model fit]*")
  # Restrict to the primary structure. Both structures are pooled into one table and
  # share a cell name up to the suffix, so an unfiltered range would silently span 36
  # fits of 18 cells and report the widest pd across two different models.
  is_max <- grepl("_itemslope$", tbl$model)
  k <- grepl(model_pattern, tbl$model) & !.is_variant(tbl$model) & tbl$parameter == term &
       (if (identical(LES_P1_PRIMARY, "maximal")) is_max else !is_max)
  p <- tbl$pd[k]
  if (!length(p)) return("*[term not found]*")
  sprintf("%s %s %s", .fmt_pd(min(p)), sep, .fmt_pd(max(p)))
}

# Median ratio of the credible-interval width WITH the by-item grammaticality slope to
# the width without it, over the ERP cells that have both fits. Injected so the
# robustness claim carries a measured number rather than an assertion that the intervals
# "did not widen much".
itemslope_width_ratio <- function(term = "z_recoded_grammaticality:z_recoded_session:z_recoded_mini_language",
                                  tbl = post_tbl) {
  if (is.null(tbl)) return("*[pending model fit]*")
  k <- tbl$parameter == term & grepl("^erp_", tbl$model) & !.is_variant(tbl$model)
  d <- tbl[k, c("model", "ci_low", "ci_high")]
  d$width <- d$ci_high - d$ci_low
  item <- d[grepl("_itemslope$", d$model), ]
  base <- d[!grepl("_itemslope$", d$model), ]
  item$base_model <- sub("_itemslope$", "", item$model)
  m <- merge(item, base, by.x = "base_model", by.y = "model", suffixes = c("_item", "_base"))
  if (!nrow(m)) return("*[pending model fit]*")
  apa_num(stats::median(m$width_item / m$width_base), digits = 2)
}

# Number of ERP cells in which `term` is credible, as "k of n". `structure` selects the
# simpler fits ("base") or the maximal by-item ones ("itemslope"), so the manuscript can
# state the sensitivity of a conclusion to the random-effect structure from the artefacts
# rather than by hand.
cred_cells <- function(term, property = "",
                       structure = if (identical(LES_P1_PRIMARY, "maximal")) "itemslope" else "base",
                       tbl = post_tbl) {
  structure <- match.arg(structure, c("base", "itemslope"))
  if (is.null(tbl)) return("*[pending model fit]*")
  # The retention-free refits carry their own suffix and are a third variant of the
  # same cells, not a random-effect structure. They must be excluded from BOTH buckets:
  # "cell_retfree" and "cell_itemslope_retfree" alike fail grepl("_itemslope$"), so
  # without this they would swell the base grid from 18 cells to 42. .is_variant() drops
  # them with every other variant.
  is_item <- grepl("_itemslope$", tbl$model)
  k <- tbl$parameter == term & grepl(paste0("^erp_", property), tbl$model) &
       !.is_variant(tbl$model) & (if (structure == "itemslope") is_item else !is_item)
  d <- tbl[k, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(d)) return("*[pending model fit]*")
  sprintf("%d of %d", sum(d$ci_low > 0 | d$ci_high < 0), nrow(d))
}

# Largest absolute credible-interval bound of `term` over one property's primary ERP cells,
# formatted. It bounds how large an effect the intervals leave room for, so a statement
# that a language term is near zero carries its own measure of precision.
term_max_bound <- function(term, property, tbl = post_tbl) {
  if (is.null(tbl)) return("*[pending model fit]*")
  want_item <- identical(LES_P1_PRIMARY, "maximal")
  k <- tbl$parameter == term & grepl(paste0("^erp_", property, "_"), tbl$model) &
       !grepl("_weakprior|_retfree|_exclreproc", tbl$model) &
       (grepl("_itemslope$", tbl$model) == want_item)
  if (!any(k)) return("*[term not found]*")
  apa_num(max(abs(c(tbl$ci_low[k], tbl$ci_high[k]))), digits = 3)
}

# Posterior probability that the Mini-Norwegian group exceeds the Mini-English group on a
# signal-detection measure at one session ("average" for the average session), from the
# derived contrast's median sign and probability of direction.
sdt_prob_mn_higher <- function(property, measure, session,
                               model = paste0("accuracy_", property)) {
  r <- .sdt_row(property, measure, "language_difference", session, model = model)
  if (is.null(r)) return("*[signal-detection contrast pending]*")
  p <- if (r$median > 0) r$pd else 1 - r$pd
  sub("^0", "", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 2))
}

# --- Reader-facing labels for the retention tables ----------------------------
# The contrast artefact carries pipeline ids ("erp_gender_agreement_400_900_midline") and
# contrast keys ("within_Mini-Norwegian"). Printed raw they read as variable names, so both
# are mapped here to the tables' vocabulary: the full property names in the order every
# other display follows, windows as "200–500 ms", and the contrasts Overall,
# Mini-Norwegian, Mini-English and Group difference. Both retention tables hold ERP rows
# only (the judgement models' retention quantities are signal-detection contrasts, in
# their own table), so every row is on one scale and no measure column is needed. An id
# or contrast key outside the known set keeps a readable form of its own label and sorts
# last, so a new variant shows up in the table instead of being dropped.
.retention_labels <- function(d) {
  m <- regmatches(d$model, regexec(
    "^erp_(.+?)_([0-9]+)_([0-9]+)_(lateral|midline)(_[a-z_]+)?$", d$model))
  part <- function(j) vapply(m, function(x) if (length(x)) x[j] else NA_character_, "")
  pkey <- part(2)
  plab <- ifelse(pkey %in% names(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_TABLE),
                 unname(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_TABLE[pkey]),
                 ifelse(is.na(pkey), d$model, gsub("_", " ", pkey)))
  w1 <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(part(3))); w2 <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(part(4)))
  win <- ifelse(is.na(w1), "", paste0(w1, "–", w2, " ms"))
  cmap <- c(overall = "Overall", `within_Mini-Norwegian` = "Mini-Norwegian",
            `within_Mini-English` = "Mini-English", language_difference = "Group difference")
  clab <- ifelse(d$contrast %in% names(cmap), unname(cmap[d$contrast]), d$contrast)
  data.frame(
    Property = factor(plab, levels = unique(c(unname(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_TABLE), plab))),
    Window   = factor(win, levels = unique(win[order(w1, w2)])),
    Region   = unname(c(lateral = "Lateral", midline = "Midline")[part(5)]),
    Contrast = factor(clab, levels = unique(c(unname(cmap), clab))),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

# Label of a full-width group or subgroup row. In the PDF it ends with \LESkeepnext
# (defined in the YAML header-includes), which stops longtable breaking the page directly
# after the row, so a group heading always has its first row beneath it. Italic marks
# the property (or model-family) group rows.
.les_group <- function(x, italic = TRUE) {
  x <- if (italic) paste0("*", x, "*") else x
  if (knitr::is_latex_output()) paste0(x, "\\LESkeepnext") else x
}

# Keep the rows of one block together in the PDF: `x` is a table's first column and
# `block` names each row's block (rows of a block are adjacent). Every row of a block but
# its last ends with \LESkeepnext, so longtable breaks a page only between blocks and a
# continuation page never opens on rows cut off from their window or contrast label.
.les_keep <- function(x, block) {
  if (!knitr::is_latex_output()) return(x)
  ifelse(duplicated(block, fromLast = TRUE), paste0(x, "\\LESkeepnext"), x)
}

# Exact column widths, as fractions of the text width, for les_grid_table(). Pandoc
# rescales a grid table's widths to the full measure whenever the grid is wider than 72
# characters, which the maths heads and \LESkeepnext marks make every table here, so the
# widths are carried by a span on the stub head instead, which
# _shared/lua/apa-table-heads.lua applies and unwraps. `docx` gives Word its own widths:
# Word sets tables at 12 pt against the PDF's 10 pt, so the same cells need more room
# there, and the fractions of both were checked against the widest cell each column can
# hold (Times New Roman metrics, with the cell padding of each output).
.les_widths <- function(header, pdf, docx = pdf) {
  stopifnot(length(pdf) == length(header), length(docx) == length(header))
  header[1] <- sprintf('[%s]{les-widths="%s" les-widths-docx="%s"}', header[1],
                       paste(pdf, collapse = " "), paste(docx, collapse = " "))
  header
}

# One layout for both retention tables (Session 4 to 6 changes, and the retention-free
# deviations): property group rows, window subgroup rows, one row per contrast, and the
# lateral and midline estimates side by side under their own spanners. Precision is one
# .les_digits value for the whole table (.fmt_est). A contrast present for one macroregion
# but not the other prints an em dash in the missing cells.
.retention_table <- function(d) {
  lb <- .retention_labels(d)
  f  <- .fmt_est(d$median, d$ci_low, d$ci_high)
  v  <- data.frame(lb, Mdn = f$median, LL = f$lo, UL = f$hi,
                   pd = ifelse(is.finite(d$pd), .fmt_pd(d$pd), "—"),
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  keys <- unique(v[, c("Property", "Window", "Contrast")])
  keys <- keys[order(keys$Property, keys$Window, keys$Contrast), , drop = FALSE]
  body <- data.frame(Contrast = .les_keep(as.character(keys$Contrast),
                                          paste(keys$Property, keys$Window)),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  for (r in c("Lateral", "Midline")) for (col in c("Mdn", "LL", "UL", "pd"))
    body[[paste(r, col)]] <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(keys)), function(i) {
      x <- v[[col]][v$Property == keys$Property[i] & v$Window == keys$Window[i] &
                      v$Contrast == keys$Contrast[i] & v$Region %in% r]
      if (length(x) == 1L) x else "—"
    }, "")
  les_grid_table(body,
    # The ERP estimates take up to four decimals and a minus sign ("−0.0124"), so the
    # estimate columns get the width. In Word (12 pt) the table needs 97% of the measure
    # for "Group difference" under two indents, "−0.0124" and "> .999" on one line each.
    header   = .les_widths(c("Contrast", rep(c("*Mdn*", "*LL*", "*UL*", "*p*~d~"), 2)),
                           pdf  = c(.24, rep(c(.10, .10, .10, .08), 2)),
                           docx = c(.229, rep(c(.1005, .1005, .1005, .0835), 2))),
    align    = c("l", rep("r", 8)),
    spanners = list(list(label = "Lateral", cols = 2:5), list(label = "Midline", cols = 6:9)),
    group    = .les_group(as.character(keys$Property)),
    subgroup = .les_group(as.character(keys$Window), italic = FALSE),
    decimals = c("Lateral pd", "Midline pd"))
}

report_contrast <- function(model_id, which = "overall", tbl = retention_tbl) {
  if (is.null(tbl)) return("*[pending model fit]*")
  model_id <- .mid(model_id)          # resolve to the primary structure
  row <- tbl[tbl$model == model_id & tbl$contrast == which, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(row) != 1) return("*[contrast not found]*")
  d <- .les_digits(row$median, row$ci_low, row$ci_high)
  sprintf("$\\Delta = %s$, 95%% CrI $[%s, %s]$, $%s$",
          apa_num(row$median, digits = d), apa_num(row$ci_low, digits = d),
          apa_num(row$ci_high, digits = d), .pd_math(row$pd))
}

# --- Between-language difference in a retention gain --------------------------
# Script 05 derives a "language_difference" contrast (Mini-Norwegian minus
# Mini-English retention change) so that any statement about the two languages'
# similarity cites an estimated quantity with its own uncertainty. Until the
# queued summaries run adds that row to _retention_contrasts.csv, the two
# within-language medians are printed with a visible marker instead, in the
# style of misfilter_status().
ret_lang_diff <- function(model_id = "erp_gender_agreement_400_900_midline",
                          freed = FALSE) {
  if (is.null(retention_tbl)) return("*[pending model fit]*")
  mid <- paste0(.mid(model_id), if (freed) "_retfree" else "")
  r <- retention_tbl[retention_tbl$model == mid &
                       retention_tbl$contrast == "language_difference", , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(r) == 1) {
    d <- .les_digits(r$median, r$ci_low, r$ci_high)
    return(sprintf(
      "Mini-Norwegian minus Mini-English $\\Delta = %s$, 95%% CrI $[%s, %s]$, $%s$",
      apa_num(r$median, digits = d), apa_num(r$ci_low, digits = d),
      apa_num(r$ci_high, digits = d), .pd_math(r$pd)))
  }
  w <- retention_tbl[retention_tbl$model == mid &
                       grepl("^within_", retention_tbl$contrast), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(w) < 2) return("*[contrast not found]*")
  paste0("within-language medians of ",
         apa_num(w$median[w$contrast == "within_Mini-Norwegian"], digits = 3), " and ",
         apa_num(w$median[w$contrast == "within_Mini-English"], digits = 3),
         "; *[between-language difference contrast pending the queued summaries run]*")
}

# --- Language modulation at the property's first session ----------------------
# With session standardised, the grammaticality x language coefficient is the
# miniature-language difference at the AVERAGE session. The first-session contrast
# estimates whether that difference was detectable at the earliest post-training
# measurement; it does not by itself identify the initial representational state.
# Script 05 derives it from the accuracy draws (b_gl + z_first * b_gsl) and writes
# results/_first_session_language_advantage.csv; reported from that artefact, with
# a visible marker until the queued summaries rerun lands.
first_adv_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_first_session_language_advantage.csv"))
first_sess_adv <- function(model_id = "accuracy_gender_agreement") {
  if (is.null(first_adv_tbl)) {
    return("*[first-session contrast pending the queued summaries run]*")
  }
  r <- first_adv_tbl[first_adv_tbl$model == model_id, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(r) != 1) return("*[first-session contrast not found]*")
  d <- .les_digits(r$median, r$ci_low, r$ci_high)
  sprintf("$b = %s$, 95%% CrI $[%s, %s]$, $%s$",
          apa_num(r$median, digits = d), apa_num(r$ci_low, digits = d),
          apa_num(r$ci_high, digits = d), .pd_math(r$pd))
}

# --- Retention-free contrasts: reporters and cell tallies ---------------------
# retfree_contrast() returns NULL when the freed fits are absent; retfree_val()
# wraps it for inline use. retfree_tally() counts, across a property's six cells,
# how many freed contrasts are credible (interval excludes zero) or share a sign,
# so statements like "positive in every cell" are computed rather than typed.
retfree_val <- function(cell_id, which = "overall") {
  est <- retfree_contrast(cell_id, which)
  if (is.null(est)) "*[retention-free contrast pending]*" else est
}
.retfree_rows <- function(property, contrast) {
  if (is.null(retention_tbl)) return(NULL)
  want_item <- identical(LES_P1_PRIMARY, "maximal")
  m <- retention_tbl
  k <- startsWith(m$model, paste0("erp_", property, "_")) &
       grepl("_retfree$", m$model) & !.is_variant(sub("_retfree$", "", m$model)) &
       (grepl("_itemslope", m$model) == want_item) & m$contrast == contrast
  r <- m[k, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(r)) NULL else r
}
retfree_tally <- function(property, contrast,
                          what = c("credible", "positive", "negative")) {
  what <- match.arg(what)
  r <- .retfree_rows(property, contrast)
  if (is.null(r)) return("*[pending]*")
  n <- switch(what,
              credible = sum(sign(r$ci_low) == sign(r$ci_high)),
              positive = sum(r$median > 0),
              negative = sum(r$median < 0))
  .word <- function(i) if (i <= 9L) c("none", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six",
                                       "seven", "eight", "nine")[i + 1L] else as.character(i)
  tot <- nrow(r)
  if (n == 0L)   return(paste0("none of the ", .word(tot)))
  if (n == tot)  return(paste0("every one of the ", .word(tot)))
  paste0(.word(n), " of the ", .word(tot))
}

# --- Retention-free refit: conditional status ---------------------------------
# LES_P1_RETENTION_FREE=1 refits a cell with an explicit Session-6 offset, so the
# linear term carries the training trend and the offset the deviation at retention
# (scripts/03_fit_brms_erp.R). Script 05 writes those contrasts into
# _retention_contrasts.csv under model ids tagged "_retfree". The consolidation
# reading in the Discussion depends on whether that refit has landed, so the
# sentence is emitted from the artefact rather than typed: once the retfree rows
# are present the freed offset is reported; until then the provisional
# linear-derivation reading is printed with a visible marker, mirroring
# misfilter_status(). The variant exists for gender agreement and differential
# object marking only: verb-object number agreement is sampled at the two
# bracketing sessions, so its linear term already is the retention change and a
# freed offset is not identifiable (script 03 refuses it).
retfree_contrast <- function(cell_id, which = "overall") {
  if (is.null(retention_tbl)) return(NULL)
  want_item <- identical(LES_P1_PRIMARY, "maximal")
  m <- retention_tbl
  k <- startsWith(m$model, cell_id) & grepl("_retfree$", m$model) &
       !.is_variant(sub("_retfree$", "", m$model)) &
       (grepl("_itemslope", m$model) == want_item) & m$contrast == which
  r <- m[k, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(r) != 1) return(NULL)
  d <- .les_digits(r$median, r$ci_low, r$ci_high)
  sprintf("$\\Delta = %s$, 95%% CrI $[%s, %s]$, $%s$",
          apa_num(r$median, digits = d), apa_num(r$ci_low, digits = d),
          apa_num(r$ci_high, digits = d), .pd_math(r$pd))
}
retfree_sentence <- function(cell_id = "erp_gender_agreement_400_900_midline") {
  est <- retfree_contrast(cell_id)
  if (!is.null(est)) {
    return(paste0(
      "A refit in which the retention step is free to differ from the training steps ",
      "separates the two readings. For this cell the freed Session-6 offset, the ",
      "deviation at retention, is ", est, "."))
  }
  paste0(
    "Separating an offline gain from continued improvement requires a model in which ",
    "the retention step is free to differ from the training steps. Such a refit is in ",
    "progress for gender agreement and differential object marking (for verb--object ",
    "number agreement, sampled at the two bracketing sessions only, the linear term ",
    "already is the direct contrast), and until its contrasts are pooled we treat ",
    "consolidation as the more plausible of two readings the linear derivation cannot ",
    "adjudicate. **[Pending: retention-free refit contrasts not yet in the pooled ",
    "summaries; re-run script 05 once the refit completes.]**")
}

# --- RSVP timing census -------------------------------------------------------
# scripts/01b_extract_rsvp_timing.R takes a census of ALL presented critical-word
# trials in the raw presentation logs, before any EEG-side exclusion: trial count, the
# distribution of the next word onset after the critical word, and the per-trial count
# of onsets within 900 ms. It writes the scalar fields (n_trials, next_onset_min_ms,
# next_onset_max_ms, next_onset_median_ms, max_onsets_within_900ms) and the per-session
# counts (n_trials_s<session>) as one row of the tracked results/_rsvp_timing.csv, and
# the full census to data_derived/rsvp_timing_overlap.rds, which is not tracked. The
# CSV is read first, as a list so that rsvp_tim() indexes it by field, and the rds is
# the fallback for a checkout that predates the CSV. Injected so the Procedure's timing
# claims track the logs rather than a hand-typed number (the typed median had already
# drifted by 1 ms from the full-census value).
.rsvp_tim <- local({
  csv <- paper1_results("_rsvp_timing.csv")
  if (file.exists(csv)) {
    as.list(utils::read.csv(csv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)[1, , drop = FALSE])
  } else {
    p <- paper1_derived("rsvp_timing_overlap.rds")
    if (file.exists(p)) readRDS(p) else NULL
  }
})
# Guard on the Method's typed "exactly one subsequent word onset falls within 900 ms": ""
# while the census's minimum and maximum onset counts are both 1 (ISSUES.md G16-10), and a
# marker otherwise, which a census over changed logs could produce.
rsvp_one_guard <- function() {
  if (is.null(.rsvp_tim)) return("")
  one <- function(f) identical(as.numeric(.rsvp_tim[[f]]), 1)
  if (one("min_onsets_within_900ms") && one("max_onsets_within_900ms")) return("")
  " **[Check: not every critical word has exactly one subsequent onset within 900 ms. Revise this sentence.]**"
}
rsvp_tim <- function(field, big = FALSE) {
  if (is.null(.rsvp_tim) || is.null(.rsvp_tim[[field]]) || !is.finite(.rsvp_tim[[field]]))
    return("*[pending timing extraction]*")
  formatC(.rsvp_tim[[field]], format = "d", big.mark = if (big) "," else "")
}

# --- Response-time filter and the legacy screen on the judgement trials ----------
# Three artefacts of 02_extract_accuracy.R, so the Method's disclosure is injected rather
# than typed:
#   * results/_accuracy_rt_screen.csv: the filter the reported data were extracted under
#     (only trials without a finite, positive response time are dropped) and its cost;
#   * _accuracy_rt_screen_rtscreen.csv: the same for the legacy (200, 4000) ms screen, the
#     sensitivity analysis;
#   * _accuracy_rt_bands.csv: the otherwise-valid trials in that screen's bands.
# Until 19 October 2026 the screen was the primary rule (ISSUES.md G06-03). Results pulled
# before the switch still carry its bounds in the primary file, and acc_rt_switch_marker()
# marks them.
.rt_tbl    <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_accuracy_rt_screen.csv"))
.rt_tbl_sc <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_accuracy_rt_screen_rtscreen.csv"))
.rt_bands  <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_accuracy_rt_bands.csv"))
rt_screen <- function(field, digits = 0, tbl = .rt_tbl) {
  if (is.null(tbl) || !field %in% names(tbl)) return("NN")
  v <- tbl[[field]][1]
  if (!is.finite(v)) return("NN")
  if (digits > 0) apa_num(v, digits = digits)
  else formatC(v, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
}
acc_rt_switch_pending <- function() {
  is.null(.rt_tbl) || !isTRUE(.rt_tbl$rt_min_ms[1] == 0) || !isTRUE(is.infinite(.rt_tbl$rt_max_ms[1]))
}
acc_rt_switch_marker <- function() {
  if (!acc_rt_switch_pending()) return("")
  paste0(" **[Pending: the judgement results still come from the fits with the reaction-time ",
         "screen; the refits on every judgement (ISSUES.md G06-03) replace them when pulled.]**")
}
# The trials the reported data drop (those without a recorded response time), as a count
# in words below ten.
rt_dropped_phrase <- function() {
  if (is.null(.rt_tbl)) return("NN")
  n <- .rt_tbl$n_rt_excluded[1]
  if (n >= 1 && n <= 9) c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight",
                          "nine")[n] else format(n, big.mark = ",")
}
# The Method's account of the legacy screen and why it is not applied: what it would remove,
# how accurate the judgements in each of its bands were, and how unequally it falls on the
# two groups. The sentences assert an order (the fast band the most accurate, the slow band
# the least) and a direction (more of the Mini-English group's judgements removed, and more
# of its fast ones), so a marker replaces them if the artefact stops showing either, or if
# the bands do not add up to the two extractions' counts.
rt_legacy_sentence <- function() {
  if (is.null(.rt_tbl) || is.null(.rt_tbl_sc) || is.null(.rt_bands)) {
    return("*[The legacy reaction-time screen's counts are pending the accuracy extraction.]*")
  }
  b <- .rt_bands[.rt_bands$band != "no_time", , drop = FALSE]
  n_sc <- .rt_tbl_sc$n_kept[1]; n_all <- .rt_tbl$n_kept[1]
  if (sum(b$n_trials) != n_all || sum(b$n_trials[b$band == "kept"]) != n_sc) {
    return(paste0(" **[Check: the response-time bands no longer add up to the trials of the two ",
                  "extractions. Rerun 02, and 02 under LES_P1_ACC_RT_SCREEN=1.]**"))
  }
  pc <- function(num, den) apa_num(100 * num / den, digits = 1)
  acc_of <- function(band) sum(b$n_correct[b$band == band]) / sum(b$n_trials[b$band == band])
  share <- function(lang, bands) {
    d <- b[b$mini_language == lang, , drop = FALSE]
    sum(d$n_trials[d$band %in% bands]) / sum(d$n_trials)
  }
  me <- share("Mini-English", c("fast", "slow")); mn <- share("Mini-Norwegian", c("fast", "slow"))
  me_f <- share("Mini-English", "fast"); mn_f <- share("Mini-Norwegian", "fast")
  if (!(acc_of("fast") > acc_of("kept") && acc_of("kept") > acc_of("slow")) ||
      !(me > mn && me_f > mn_f)) {
    return(paste0(" **[Check: the legacy screen's bands no longer show the accuracy order or ",
                  "the group imbalance this paragraph describes. Revise it.]**"))
  }
  lo <- rt_screen("rt_min_ms", tbl = .rt_tbl_sc); hi <- rt_screen("rt_max_ms", tbl = .rt_tbl_sc)
  paste0(
    "The project's earlier preprocessing also discarded judgements of ", lo, " ms or less or of ",
    hi, " ms or more. That screen removes a further ", format(n_all - n_sc, big.mark = ","),
    " trials (", pc(n_all - n_sc, n_all), "%), and we do not apply it, for three reasons. Its ",
    "bounds have no recorded rationale. It selects on the outcome. The judgement was requested ",
    "only after the sentence had ended, so a response within ", lo, " ms of the request was a ",
    "decision already made, and these responses were the most accurate in the data (",
    pc(acc_of("fast"), 1), "% correct), whereas those of ", hi, " ms or more were the least ",
    "accurate (", pc(acc_of("slow"), 1), "%), against ", pc(acc_of("kept"), 1), "% for the ",
    "judgements the screen keeps. And it does not fall on the two groups alike: it removes ",
    pc(me, 1), "% of the Mini-English group's judgements and ", pc(mn, 1), "% of the ",
    "Mini-Norwegian group's, mostly through the fast responses (", pc(me_f, 1), "% against ",
    pc(mn_f, 1), "%). The Results report the accuracy models refitted with the screen as a ",
    "sensitivity analysis.")
}

# Session 4 logfiles the accuracy extraction cannot read (results/_accuracy_input_gaps.csv,
# a census script 02 writes without changing what it extracts). Two export formats are
# affected, and the participants concerned contribute no Session 4 judgements. The census
# has a third reason, unread_extra_export: a suffixed export beside a complete plain log of
# the same run, which loses nothing and is left out of the sentence. The sentence names two
# features and one session, so it checks both against the census and prints a marker if a
# re-extraction finds another reason, another session, or only one of the two.
.gap_tbl <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_accuracy_input_gaps.csv"))
acc_gap_sentence <- function() {
  if (is.null(.gap_tbl)) {
    return(paste0("Two features of the Session 4 logs removed further judgements ",
                  "*[counts pending the accuracy extraction]*."))
  }
  lost <- .gap_tbl[.gap_tbl$reason %in% c("split_export", "semicolon_delimited"), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!all(.gap_tbl$reason %in% c("split_export", "semicolon_delimited", "unread_extra_export")) ||
      !identical(sort(unique(as.character(lost$session))), "4") ||
      !setequal(unique(lost$reason), c("split_export", "semicolon_delimited"))) {
