## The trials the trigger rule discards

The two-step segmentation described in the Method keeps a critical word only when its
condition trigger followed its property trigger by exactly five samples, and about a third of
the words failed that rule. Fewer trials lower precision, but they bias the grammaticality
contrast only if the discarded trials differ from the kept ones within a condition. The
reprocessing protocol fixed a check of that assumption before any reprocessed output was
inspected, on the seventeen recordings whose discarded epochs could be rebuilt from the raw
data: the nine reprocessed Session 3 records and eight 0.1 Hz recordings rebuilt for the
filter validation, four from Session 2 and four from Session 3. Each recording was first
rebuilt and checked against its archived exports. Every grammatical and ungrammatical epoch
was then locked to the word-onset trigger ($-96$ to 1,096 ms), and each window mean was
adjusted for the pre-stimulus baseline within each recording, as the ERP models adjust it.
In each property, window and macroregion, the check estimates $D$, the difference between
discarded and kept trials in the ungrammatical-minus-grammatical contrast, weighting the
recordings equally. Omitting the discarded trials shifts the analysed contrast by the
discarded share times $D$, so the check passes where the 90% interval of $D$ lies within
$\pm 0.91$ µV (two one-sided tests at $\alpha = .05$), which keeps that shift within about
0.33 µV. `r trigger_check_sentence()` The check has about 80% power for a single cell, and
much less for all of them jointly, so a pass bounds gross differences without establishing
that the two sets of trials are equivalent. It admits no trial to any analysis.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-trigger-check
#| tbl-cap: "Discarded Against Kept Trials in the Ungrammatical-Minus-Grammatical Contrast"
#| apa-note: "*D* = difference between the trials the five-sample trigger rule discards and the trials it keeps in the ungrammatical-minus-grammatical contrast of the window mean (µV), locked to the word-onset trigger and adjusted for the pre-stimulus baseline within each recording, averaged over recordings with equal weight. *k* = recordings; Kept and Discarded = grammatical and ungrammatical trials in each set. *LL* and *UL* = limits of the 90% interval of the two one-sided tests; a cell passes where both lie within ±0.91 µV. Gender agreement is recorded at Sessions 2 and 3 and differential object marking at Session 3, so the two properties draw on different recordings."
#| apa-longtable: false
.td <- .trig_primary()
if (!is.null(.td) && has_knitr) {
  .td <- .td[order(match(.td$property, names(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_TABLE)), .td$window,
                   .td$macroregion), ]
  .f <- .fmt_est(.td$D_int, .td$ci90_low, .td$ci90_high)
  .body <- data.frame(
    Cell = paste0(sub("_", "–", .td$window), " ms, ", .td$macroregion),
    k = as.character(.td$n_recordings),
    Kept = format(.td$n_kept, big.mark = ","), Discarded = format(.td$n_discarded, big.mark = ","),
    D = .f$median, LL = .f$lo, UL = .f$hi,
    Passes = ifelse(.td$passes, "Yes", "No"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  les_grid_table(.body,
    header = .les_widths(c("Window and macroregion", "*k*", "Kept", "Discarded", "*D*", "*LL*",
                           "*UL*", "Within bound"),
                         pdf = c(.25, .05, .09, .11, .11, .11, .11, .14),
                         docx = c(.25, .05, .09, .12, .11, .11, .11, .14)),
    align = c("l", rep("r", 6), "l"),
    spanners = list(list(label = "90% interval", cols = 6:7)),
    group = .les_group(unname(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_TABLE[.td$property])))
} else {
  knitr::asis_output("*The trigger-rule check will appear here once it has run.*")
}
```

## The decoding correction family

The Method states how the second layer of multiplicity control on the decoding analyses
is defined. Correcting instead across the pooled, per-session and
per-session-by-language cells of one property would span nested, overlapping re-analyses
of the same trials. Across those, the number of hypotheses is not well defined, and the
positive-dependence condition that licenses Benjamini--Hochberg under dependence cannot
be established. A false-discovery rate computed over such a family is not interpretable.
The three properties' pooled time-courses rest on disjoint sets of trials, and correcting
each property's family separately keeps every family self-contained.

Within a property, the second layer adds no error control to the maximum-cluster test.
That test controls the family-wise error rate across the time-course, in the sense the
Results describe, and the false-discovery rate cannot exceed it. A Benjamini--Hochberg
adjustment never lowers a $p$ value, so applied to these values it can only remove
clusters. The layer was specified, and stated in the Method, before the decoding of the
corrected sample was run. That it adds no error control was noted in an audit of the
analysis code before that run, and the decision to keep it was taken once the corrected
results were available. We keep it so that no decision rests on a correction chosen after
those results were seen. Its cost is visible wherever it matters, because the clusters that
pass the maximum-cluster test are reported beside those that survive both layers. For
gender agreement, it is what separates `r dec_count(dec_gender, "n_overall_fwer", "cluster")`
that pass the first test from none that survive both.`r dec_m_sentence()``r dec_appx_guard()`
The family itself was narrowed to the pooled time-course in July 2026, after a run under
the wider family had been inspected, for the reasons given above.`r decode_status_appendix()`

# Retention contrasts in full {#apx-retention-tables}

The Results report the contrasts that carry the argument. The three tables below give the
full record: every Session 4 to Session 6 contrast of the reported ERP models
(@tbl-retention), every retention-free contrast from the refits that carry an explicit
retention indicator (@tbl-retention-free), and the sensitivity and criterion contrasts
derived from the judgement models (@tbl-sdt-contrasts). All three are read from the pooled
summary artefacts and reproduce with them.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-retention
#| tbl-cap: "Change in the ERP Grammaticality Effect From Session 4 to Session 6"
#| apa-note: "Values are posterior summaries of the change in the ERP grammaticality effect from Session 4 to Session 6 in the reported models, in within-participant standard-deviation units of amplitude. Positive values indicate an effect that strengthened over the interval. Overall = averaged over the two groups; Group difference = Mini-Norwegian minus Mini-English. *Mdn* = posterior median; *LL* and *UL* = lower and upper limits of the 95% equal-tailed credible interval; *p*~d~ = probability of direction. An em dash marks a contrast not yet available. The judgement models' retention quantities are reported in signal-detection terms with the sensitivity and criterion contrasts in this appendix."
#| apa-longtable: true
if (!is.null(retention_tbl) && has_knitr) {
  # As with the forest plot, restrict to the reported fits: the artefact carries all four
  # variants of every cell, and printed whole it made a 225-row table in which the
  # reported rows could not be told from the sensitivity ones.
  # ERP rows only. For the accuracy models, the change in the grammaticality coefficient is
  # a change in response bias, so their retention quantities are reported in signal-
  # detection terms in the sensitivity and criterion table instead.
  rtb <- retention_tbl |>
    filter(grepl("^erp_", model), !.is_variant(model),
           model == vapply(sub("_itemslope$", "", model), .mid, ""))
  if (nrow(rtb)) .retention_table(rtb) else
    knitr::asis_output("*The ERP retention contrasts are withheld until the models are refitted.*")
} else {
  knitr::asis_output("*Retention contrasts will appear here once the models are fitted.*")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-retention-free
#| tbl-cap: "Deviation of the ERP Grammaticality Effect at Session 6 From the Training Trend (Retention-Free Refits)"
#| apa-note: "Values are posterior summaries of the deviation of the grammaticality effect at Session 6 from the trend established across the training sessions, from refits that carry an explicit retention indicator (coded +0.5 at Session 6), in within-participant standard-deviation units of amplitude. Positive values mean that the grammaticality coefficient at Session 6 exceeds the value the training trend predicts; because a positive grammaticality coefficient is a relative negativity for violations, a positive deviation shifts the effect towards violation negativity. Verb--object number agreement is omitted because its indicator is not identifiable. Overall = averaged over the two groups; Group difference = Mini-Norwegian minus Mini-English. *Mdn*, *LL*, *UL* and *p*~d~ are as in the table of Session 4 to Session 6 changes."
#| apa-longtable: true
if (!is.null(retention_tbl) && has_knitr) {
  want_item <- identical(LES_P1_PRIMARY, "maximal")
  rtf <- retention_tbl |>
    filter(grepl("_retfree$", model), !.is_variant(sub("_retfree$", "", model)),
           grepl("_itemslope", model) == want_item)
  if (nrow(rtf)) .retention_table(rtf) else
    knitr::asis_output("*The retention-free contrasts will appear here once the refits are pooled.*")
} else {
  knitr::asis_output("*Retention-free contrasts will appear here once the models are fitted.*")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sdt-contrasts
#| tbl-cap: "Group Differences and Changes in Sensitivity and Criterion From the Judgement Models"
#| apa-note: "Values are posterior summaries derived from the draws of the reported accuracy models (see *Signal-detection reading of the judgement models*): sensitivity *d*~L~ on the logit scale, and criterion *c*~L~, negative for a readiness to answer grammatical. Group differences are Mini-Norwegian minus Mini-English, at each session and averaged over sessions. Changes run from the property's first session to Session 6, for each group and as the group difference in that change. *Mdn* = posterior median; *LL* and *UL* = lower and upper limits of the 95% equal-tailed credible interval; *p*~d~ = probability of direction."
#| apa-longtable: true
if (!is.null(sdt_tbl) && has_knitr) {
  st <- sdt_tbl[sdt_tbl$model %in% paste0("accuracy_", names(LES_P1_PROPERTIES)) &
                  sdt_tbl$contrast %in% c("language_difference", "change_first_to_last",
                                          "change_first_to_last_language_difference"), ]
  st$prop <- sub("^accuracy_", "", st$model)
  # Two blocks per property: the group difference at each session and averaged over
  # sessions, then the change from the property's first session to Session 6, whose
  # session key ("2->6", "3->6", "4->6") names both ends.
  is_diff  <- st$contrast == "language_difference"
  st$block <- ifelse(is_diff, "Group difference (Mini-Norwegian minus Mini-English)",
                     sub("^([0-9]+)->([0-9]+)$", "Change from Session \\1 to Session \\2",
                         st$session))
  st$row <- ifelse(is_diff,
                   ifelse(st$session == "average", "Averaged over sessions",
                          paste("Session", st$session)),
                   ifelse(st$contrast == "change_first_to_last", st$mini_language,
                          "Group difference"))
  # One precision for the whole table (both measures), with true minus signs.
  .f <- .fmt_est(st$median, st$ci_low, st$ci_high)
  st$Mdn <- .f$median; st$LL <- .f$lo; st$UL <- .f$hi
  st$pdf <- ifelse(is.finite(st$pd), .fmt_pd(st$pd), "—")
  st$key <- paste(st$prop, st$block, st$row, sep = "|")
  rows <- c(paste("Session", LES_ERP_SESSIONS), "Averaged over sessions",
            "Mini-Norwegian", "Mini-English", "Group difference")
  keys <- unique(st[, c("key", "prop", "block", "row")])
  keys <- keys[order(match(keys$prop, names(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_TABLE)),
                     !startsWith(keys$block, "Group"), keys$block,
                     match(keys$row, rows)), , drop = FALSE]
  body <- data.frame(Contrast = .les_keep(keys$row, paste(keys$prop, keys$block)),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  for (m in c("sensitivity", "criterion")) for (col in c("Mdn", "LL", "UL", "pdf"))
    body[[paste(m, col)]] <- vapply(keys$key, function(k) {
      v <- st[[col]][st$key == k & st$measure == m]
      if (length(v) == 1L) v else "—"
    }, "", USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  les_grid_table(body,
    # Wide enough for "Averaged over sessions" under two indents, "−10.12" and "> .999"
    # on one line each, also in Word (12 pt), where the table needs 95% of the measure.
    header   = .les_widths(c("Contrast", rep(c("*Mdn*", "*LL*", "*UL*", "*p*~d~"), 2)),
                           pdf  = c(.30, rep(c(.09, .09, .09, .08), 2)),
                           docx = c(.30, rep(c(.0885, .0885, .0885, .0845), 2))),
    align    = c("l", rep("r", 8)),
    spanners = list(list(label = "Sensitivity (*d*~L~)", cols = 2:5),
                    list(label = "Criterion (*c*~L~)", cols = 6:9)),
    group    = .les_group(unname(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_TABLE[keys$prop])),
    subgroup = .les_group(keys$block, italic = FALSE),
    decimals = c("sensitivity pdf", "criterion pdf"))
} else {
  knitr::asis_output("*Signal-detection contrasts will appear here once the summaries have run.*")
}
```

# Prior specifications {#apx-prior-specifications}

The reasoning behind each prior is given in the Method, under *Priors*. What follows is the
specification itself. Every mean and standard deviation is on the standardised scale, so a
coefficient is in standard-deviation units, within participant for the ERP models. Prior
means encode a direction and a regularised magnitude only, never a literature effect size,
because the sources do not supply a transferable one. A directional prior is placed only
where the literature supports a sign. Everything else, including the grammaticality slope
in the 200--500 ms window, differential object marking at 300--600 ms and the
language-conditioned interaction under test, takes the model's zero-centred default.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-priors
#| tbl-cap: "Prior Distributions of the ERP and Judgement-Accuracy Models"
#| apa-note: "Informative = the literature-derived priors of the reported models; Weak = the weakly informative baseline of the prior-sensitivity refits. Zero-centred entries carry no directional claim, and the standard deviation is what bounds a prior's influence. *N*(*μ*, *σ*) = normal distribution with mean *μ* and standard deviation *σ*; half-*t*(*ν*, 0, *σ*) = Student-*t* distribution with *ν* degrees of freedom and scale *σ*, truncated at zero; LKJ(*η*) = Lewandowski--Kurowicka--Joe distribution over correlation matrices with shape *η*. All coefficients are on the standardised scale."
#| apa-longtable: true
# Generated by calling the prior builders the models were fitted with, rather than
# transcribed: les_priors_gaussian() and les_priors_bernoulli() for the informative set and
# their _weak counterparts for the baseline, all in _shared/R/01_bayesian_settings.R. They
# are called directly, not through les_erp_prior()/les_acc_prior(), whose output depends on
# the LES_PRIOR_SET variable of the rendering session, so the two columns always show both
# sets. The builders are pure functions of (window, property), so the table cannot drift
# from the fitted specification: change a prior there and this table changes with it.
# Transcribing them by hand had once introduced three wrong values, because a directional
# prior is emitted only where its mean is non-zero and the zero-centred cases fall back to
# the class default, which reading the prose did not reveal. Each row therefore looks its
# prior up by class and coefficient and falls back to the class default, as brms does, and
# checks that every ERP cell it stands for gives the same prior. A coefficient-specific
# prior that no row names is appended as a row of its own, so none can be left out.
.priors_ok <- has_knitr && requireNamespace("brms", quietly = TRUE) &&
  file.exists(here::here("_shared", "R", "01_bayesian_settings.R"))
if (.priors_ok) {
  # The settings file announces the backend and threading with cat(), which chunk options
  # cannot suppress because it is printed output rather than a message; unwrapped, that
  # banner rendered as a stray line of console text in this appendix.
  invisible(utils::capture.output(suppressPackageStartupMessages(
    source(here::here("_shared", "R", "01_bayesian_settings.R")))))
  .erp  <- "ERP models (Gaussian likelihood)"
  .acc  <- "Judgement-accuracy models (Bernoulli likelihood, logit link)"
  .props <- names(LES_P1_PROPERTIES)
  .wins  <- c("200_500", "300_600", "400_900")
  .agree <- setdiff(.props, "differential_object_marking")
  .cells <- function(w, p) expand.grid(w = w, p = p, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  .all   <- .cells(.wins, .props)
  .win_lab <- function(w) paste0(sub("_", "–", w), " ms")
  # family, parameter label, brms class and coef, and the ERP cells (window x property)
  # the row stands for; the accuracy builders take no window and ignore the property.
  .spec <- list(
    list(.erp, "Intercept", "Intercept", "", .all),
    list(.erp, paste("Grammaticality, agreement properties,", .win_lab("300_600")),
         "b", "z_recoded_grammaticality", .cells("300_600", .agree)),
    list(.erp, paste("Grammaticality, agreement properties,", .win_lab("400_900")),
         "b", "z_recoded_grammaticality", .cells("400_900", .agree)),
    list(.erp, paste("Grammaticality, differential object marking,", .win_lab("400_900")),
         "b", "z_recoded_grammaticality", .cells("400_900", "differential_object_marking")),
    list(.erp, "All other coefficients", "b", "", .all),
    list(.erp, "Residual standard deviation", "sigma", "", .all),
    list(.erp, "Random-effect standard deviations", "sd", "", .all),
    list(.erp, "Random-effect correlations", "cor", "", .all),
    list(.acc, "Intercept", "Intercept", "", NULL),
    list(.acc, "Session", "b", "z_recoded_session", NULL),
    list(.acc, "All other coefficients", "b", "", NULL),
    list(.acc, "Random-effect standard deviations", "sd", "", NULL),
    list(.acc, "Random-effect correlations", "cor", "", NULL))
  .lookup <- function(pr, class, coef) {
    pr <- as.data.frame(pr)
    k <- pr$class == class & pr$coef == coef
    if (!any(k)) k <- pr$class == class & pr$coef == ""
    if (any(k)) pr$prior[which(k)[1]] else NA_character_
  }
  # The builder output for the cells a row stands for (every property for the accuracy
  # models); more than one distinct prior means the row mislabels its cells, and both are
  # printed so that it shows.
  .prior_of <- function(s, weak) {
    v <- if (identical(s[[1]], .erp)) {
      f <- if (weak) les_priors_gaussian_weak else les_priors_gaussian
      mapply(function(w, p) .lookup(f(window = w, property = p), s[[3]], s[[4]]),
             s[[5]]$w, s[[5]]$p)
    } else {
      f <- if (weak) les_priors_bernoulli_weak else les_priors_bernoulli
      vapply(.props, function(p) .lookup(f(property = p), s[[3]], s[[4]]), "")
    }
    paste(unique(v), collapse = " / ")
  }
  # Markdown, not maths: italic N and t, and a true minus through les_grid_table(). A
  # half-t is Student-t on a standard-deviation class, which brms bounds at zero. The
  # italic N is written with underscores because a cell that starts with an asterisk is
  # escaped as a list marker.
  .fmt_prior <- function(p, class) {
    if (is.na(p) || !nzchar(p)) return("—")
    if (grepl("^normal\\(", p)) return(sub("^normal\\((.*)\\)$", "_N_(\\1)", p))
    if (grepl("^student_t\\(", p))
      return(sub("^student_t\\((.*)\\)$",
                 if (class %in% c("sd", "sigma")) "half-*t*(\\1)" else "_t_(\\1)", p))
    if (grepl("^lkj\\(", p)) return(sub("^lkj\\((.*)\\)$", "LKJ(\\1)", p))
    p
  }
  pr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(.spec, function(s) data.frame(
    model = s[[1]], Parameter = s[[2]],
    Informative = .fmt_prior(.prior_of(s, FALSE), s[[3]]),
    Weak        = .fmt_prior(.prior_of(s, TRUE),  s[[3]]), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
  # Coverage: every coefficient-specific informative ERP prior on the fitted grid must be
  # stood for by a row naming that coefficient and cell.
  .named <- do.call(rbind, lapply(Filter(function(s) identical(s[[1]], .erp) && nzchar(s[[4]]),
                                         .spec), function(s) cbind(s[[5]], coef = s[[4]])))
  .miss <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(.all)), function(i) {
    d <- as.data.frame(les_priors_gaussian(window = .all$w[i], property = .all$p[i]))
    d <- d[nzchar(d$coef), , drop = FALSE]
    if (!nrow(d)) return(NULL)
    d <- d[!paste(.all$w[i], .all$p[i], d$coef) %in% paste(.named$w, .named$p, .named$coef), ,
           drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(d)) data.frame(
      model = .erp,
      Parameter = paste0(d$coef, ", ", .win_lab(.all$w[i]), ", ", gsub("_", " ", .all$p[i])),
      Informative = vapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), function(j) .fmt_prior(d$prior[j], d$class[j]), ""),
      Weak = .fmt_prior(.lookup(les_priors_gaussian_weak(), "b", ""), "b"),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
  if (!is.null(.miss) && nrow(.miss)) {
    warning("tbl-priors: coefficient-specific priors without a table row were appended")
    k <- max(which(pr$model == .erp))
    pr <- rbind(pr[seq_len(k), ], .miss, pr[-seq_len(k), ])
  }
  les_grid_table(pr[, c("Parameter", "Informative", "Weak")],
                 # The longest parameter label ("Grammaticality, differential object
                 # marking, 400–900 ms") stays on one line in both outputs: about 5.6 in of
                 # the measure in the PDF, and the full measure in Word (12 pt).
                 header = .les_widths(c("Parameter", "Informative", "Weak"),
                                      pdf = c(.55, .16, .16), docx = c(.63, .185, .185)),
                 align = c("l", "l", "l"),
                 spanners = list(list(label = "Prior", cols = 2:3)),
                 group = .les_group(pr$model))
} else {
  knitr::asis_output(paste("*The prior specifications are generated from the shared",
                           "Bayesian settings and appear here when brms is available.*"))
}
```

# Convergence diagnostics {#apx-convergence-diagnostics}

This appendix reports the realised sampling diagnostics for every fitted model. Each of
the 18 ERP cells was fitted under two random-effect structures (base and maximal) and
two prior sets, the literature-derived informative priors reported throughout and the
weakly informative baseline used for the sensitivity analysis, giving
`r conv_n("^erp_.*(lateral|midline)(_weakprior)?(_itemslope)?$")` grid fits. Each of the
3 accuracy models was fitted under the two prior sets with its reported by-participant
structure, giving
`r conv_n("^accuracy_(differential_object_marking|gender_agreement|verb_object_number_agreement)(_weakprior)?$")` fits.
The retention-free refits add
`r conv_n("(lateral|midline)(_itemslope)?_retfree$")` fits, the 12 gender-agreement and differential-object-marking
cells under both structures with the informative
priors. `r acc_refits_sentence()`
The diversity score is not the covariate the ERP models carry, which is the L1 dominance
score of the same questionnaire, so this refit does not remedy the asymmetry noted in the
Method. The robustness analysis of the reprocessing protocol adds
`r conv_n("_exclreproc")` ERP fits, the 18 cells refitted without the reprocessed and
recovered records under the maximal structure and the informative
priors.`r if (!is.null(conv_tbl) && any(grepl("_exclreproc|_diversity|_rtscreen|_nortscreen", conv_tbl$model))) " The data-side sensitivity variants are identified in the tables' Fit column." else ""`
In all, `r if (is.null(conv_tbl)) "NN" else nrow(conv_tbl)` models were fitted, and the five
groups above account for every one of them.
@tbl-convergence-appendix (ERP models) and @tbl-convergence-accuracy (judgement-accuracy
models) give the realised diagnostics for every one, so a
model that converged comfortably can be told from one that converged marginally.

```{r}
#| include: false
# Shared by the two convergence tables below (ERP fits, then judgement-accuracy fits).
# Each fitted model appears exactly once across the two tables: an id is parsed into its
# design fields and its run tags, the ERP fits of the two random-effect structures sit
# side by side on one row, and a tag this code does not know is printed in the Fit column
# (never folded into the property), so a new variant shows up instead of vanishing.
# Structure is read off the id, the field every other accessor in this manuscript treats
# as authoritative for the random-effect structure.
.conv_is_erp <- function(model) startsWith(model, "erp_")
.conv_failed <- function(d) !is.na(d$passed) & !d$passed
.conv_any_failed <- function(erp) !is.null(conv_tbl) &&
  any(.conv_failed(conv_tbl[.conv_is_erp(conv_tbl$model) == erp, , drop = FALSE]))
# R-hat to three decimals, marked with a superscript a when the model failed any of the
# criteria (which were applied to the unrounded values). In a column that holds a mark,
# the unmarked values carry an invisible one of the same width (a phantom in the PDF, a
# superscript figure space in Word), so the digits stay aligned.
.conv_rhat <- function(d) ifelse(is.na(d$max_rhat), "—",
  paste0(les_num(d$max_rhat, 3), ifelse(.conv_failed(d), "^a^", "")))
.conv_ess <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "—", les_int(x))
.conv_align_marks <- function(x) {
  if (!any(endsWith(x, "^a^"))) return(x)
  ph <- if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "^\\phantom{a}^" else paste0("^", intToUtf8(0x2007), "^")
  k <- grepl("[0-9]$", x)
  x[k] <- paste0(x[k], ph)
  x
}
.conv_tags <- function(rest) lapply(strsplit(sub("^_", "", rest), "_", fixed = TRUE),
                                    function(t) t[nzchar(t)])
# The notes. A list-form note puts the specific note on its own line (APA 7); the
# specific note is printed only for a table that has a marked value, and the definition of
# the reprocessed-excluded refit only when that refit exists. Each note defines every
# abbreviation and criterion its table uses, so either table can be read on its own.
.conv_defs <- paste(
  "$\\widehat{R}$ = largest rank-normalised $\\widehat{R}$; Bulk and Tail = smallest bulk",
  "and tail effective sample size (ESS), each over all parameters of the model.",
  "$\\widehat{R}$ is rounded to three decimals; the criteria ($\\widehat{R}$ < 1.01, both",
  "ESS > 400, no divergent transitions) were applied before rounding.")
.conv_note_erp <- function() c(
  paste0(
    "Maximal structure = the reported by-participant and by-item random-effect structure; ",
    "Base structure = the same without the by-item grammaticality slope. Informative prior = ",
    "the reported priors; Weak prior = the weakly informative baseline; Retention-free = the ",
    "refit that frees the Session-6 step from the training trend (informative priors).",
    if (!is.null(conv_tbl) && any(grepl("_exclreproc", conv_tbl$model)))
      paste(" Reprocessed excluded = the robustness refit that leaves out the nine",
            "reprocessed Session 3 recordings and the two recovered records."),
    " ", .conv_defs, " An em dash marks a fit whose diagnostics are not yet available."),
  if (.conv_any_failed(TRUE)) "^a^ Did not meet the convergence criteria.")
.conv_note_acc <- function() {
  a <- if (is.null(conv_tbl)) NULL else conv_tbl[!.conv_is_erp(conv_tbl$model), , drop = FALSE]
  pending <- !is.null(a) && anyNA(a[, c("max_rhat", "min_ess_bulk", "min_ess_tail")])
  c(paste("Informative prior = the reported model; Weak prior = the weakly informative",
          "baseline. The other refits, all under the informative priors, add a by-participant",
          "grammaticality × session slope, the LHQ3 Multilingual Language Diversity Score as a",
          "covariate, the crossed by-item term of the ERP models or both the slope and that",
          "term, or apply the reaction-time screen of the earlier preprocessing.", .conv_defs,
          if (pending) "An em dash marks a fit whose diagnostics are not yet available."),
    if (.conv_any_failed(FALSE)) "^a^ Did not meet the convergence criteria.")
}
```

```{=latex}
% The two convergence tables run to more than a page between them, so their rows are set
% at the single-spaced pitch of the table font (reset after the second table).
\renewcommand{\LESarraystretch}{1}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-convergence-appendix
#| tbl-cap: "Convergence Diagnostics for the ERP Models"
#| apa-note: !expr .conv_note_erp()
#| apa-longtable: true
.e <- if (is.null(conv_tbl)) NULL else conv_tbl[.conv_is_erp(conv_tbl$model), , drop = FALSE]
if (!is.null(.e) && nrow(.e) && has_knitr) {
  # "erp_<property>_<start>_<end>_<region>" followed by the run tags, which compose in the
  # order _exclreproc, _weakprior, _itemslope, _retfree (paper_1_transfer/hpc/README.md).
  m <- regmatches(.e$model, regexec(
    "^erp_(.+?)_([0-9]{3})_([0-9]{3})_(lateral|midline)((_[a-z]+)*)$", .e$model))
  part <- function(j) vapply(m, function(x) if (length(x)) x[j] else NA_character_, "")
  pkey <- part(2); ok <- !is.na(pkey)
  tags <- .conv_tags(ifelse(ok, part(6), ""))
  .e$prop <- ifelse(!ok, "Other ERP models",
                    ifelse(pkey %in% names(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_TABLE),
                           unname(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_TABLE[pkey]), gsub("_", " ", pkey)))
  .e$win  <- ifelse(ok, paste0(part(3), "–", part(4)), "")
  .e$reg  <- ifelse(ok, unname(c(lateral = "Lateral", midline = "Midline")[part(5)]), "")
  .e$struct <- vapply(tags, function(t) if ("itemslope" %in% t) "maximal" else "base", "")
  fit_lv <- c("Informative prior", "Weak prior", "Retention-free")
  .e$fit_base <- vapply(tags, function(t)
    if ("retfree" %in% t) "Retention-free" else if ("weakprior" %in% t) "Weak prior"
    else "Informative prior", "")
  .e$fit <- mapply(function(b, t, id, ok) {
    if (!ok) return(sub("^erp_", "", id))
    extra <- c(if ("retfree" %in% t && "weakprior" %in% t) "weak prior",
               if ("exclreproc" %in% t) "reprocessed excluded",
               setdiff(t, c("exclreproc", "weakprior", "itemslope", "retfree")))
    paste(c(b, extra), collapse = ", ")
  }, .e$fit_base, tags, .e$model, ok)
  .e$R <- .conv_rhat(.e)
  .e$B <- .conv_ess(.e$min_ess_bulk)
  .e$T <- .conv_ess(.e$min_ess_tail)
  .e$key <- paste(.e$prop, .e$win, .e$reg, .e$fit, sep = "|")
  k <- unique(.e[, c("key", "prop", "win", "reg", "fit", "fit_base")])
  k <- k[order(match(k$prop, c(unname(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_TABLE), "Other ERP models")), k$prop,
               k$win, match(k$reg, c("Lateral", "Midline")),
               match(k$fit_base, fit_lv), k$fit), , drop = FALSE]
  cell <- function(key, s, col) {
    v <- .e[[col]][.e$key == key & .e$struct == s]
    if (length(v) == 1L) v else if (!length(v)) "—" else paste(v, collapse = " / ")
  }
  pw  <- paste(k$prop, k$win)
  # Window and Region print on the first row of their block only, so a window's rows are
  # kept on one page (.les_keep): a continuation page then opens with its window label.
  body <- data.frame(Window = .les_keep(ifelse(!duplicated(pw), k$win, ""), pw),
                     Region = ifelse(!duplicated(paste(pw, k$reg)), k$reg, ""),
                     Fit = k$fit, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  for (s in c("maximal", "base")) for (col in c("R", "B", "T"))
    body[[paste(s, col)]] <- vapply(k$key, cell, "", s = s, col = col, USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  body[["maximal R"]] <- .conv_align_marks(body[["maximal R"]])
  body[["base R"]]    <- .conv_align_marks(body[["base R"]])
  if (sum(table(paste(.e$key, .e$struct)) == 1L) != nrow(.e))
    warning("tbl-convergence-appendix: two fits share one table cell")
  les_grid_table(body,
    # "Window (ms)", "Informative prior", "1.011^a^" and "10,127" stay on one line in both
    # outputs; Word (12 pt) needs 93% of the measure.
    header   = .les_widths(c("Window (ms)", "Region", "Fit",
                             rep(c("$\\widehat{R}$", "Bulk", "Tail"), 2)),
                           pdf = c(.16, .10, .20, .09, .0875, .0875, .09, .0875, .0875)),
    align    = c("l", "l", "l", rep("r", 6)),
    spanners = list(list(label = "Maximal structure", cols = 4:6),
                    list(label = "Base structure", cols = 7:9)),
    group    = .les_group(k$prop))
} else {
  knitr::asis_output("*Convergence diagnostics will appear here once the models are fitted.*")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-convergence-accuracy
#| tbl-cap: "Convergence Diagnostics for the Judgement-Accuracy Models"
#| apa-note: !expr .conv_note_acc()
#| apa-longtable: true
.a <- if (is.null(conv_tbl)) NULL else conv_tbl[!.conv_is_erp(conv_tbl$model), , drop = FALSE]
if (!is.null(.a) && nrow(.a) && has_knitr) {
  # "accuracy_<property>" followed by the run tags. The property is the longest known key
  # the stem starts with, so an unknown tag lands in the Fit column.
  stem <- sub("^accuracy_", "", .a$model)
  pkey <- vapply(stem, function(s) {
    h <- names(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_TABLE)[startsWith(s, names(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_TABLE))]
    if (length(h)) h[which.max(nchar(h))] else NA_character_
  }, "", USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  ok <- startsWith(.a$model, "accuracy_") & !is.na(pkey)
  tags <- .conv_tags(ifelse(ok, substring(stem, nchar(pkey) + 1L), ""))
  .a$prop <- ifelse(ok, unname(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_TABLE[pkey]), "Other models")
  fit_lv <- c("Informative prior", "Weak prior",
              "Grammaticality × session slope added", "Language-diversity covariate added",
              "By-item term added", "Reaction-time screen applied")
  .a$fit <- mapply(function(t, id, ok) {
    if (!ok) return(id)
    lab <- c(if ("weakprior" %in% t) fit_lv[2], if ("maxranef" %in% t) fit_lv[3],
             if ("diversity" %in% t) fit_lv[4], if ("byitem" %in% t) fit_lv[5],
             if ("rtscreen" %in% t) fit_lv[6],
             setdiff(t, c("weakprior", "maxranef", "diversity", "byitem", "rtscreen")))
    if (!length(lab)) return(fit_lv[1])
    # Several changes read as one label ("Grammaticality × session slope and by-item term
    # added"), not as capitalised labels run together.
    if (length(lab) > 1L) {
      lab[-1] <- paste0(tolower(substr(lab[-1], 1, 1)), substring(lab[-1], 2))
      if (all(endsWith(lab, " added")))
        lab[-length(lab)] <- sub(" added$", "", lab[-length(lab)])
    }
    sub(", ([^,]*)$", " and \\1", paste(lab, collapse = ", "))
  }, tags, .a$model, ok)
  .a <- .a[order(match(.a$prop, c(unname(LES_PROPERTY_LABELS_TABLE), "Other models")),
                 match(.a$fit, fit_lv), .a$fit), , drop = FALSE]
  body <- data.frame(Fit = .les_keep(.a$fit, .a$prop), R = .conv_align_marks(.conv_rhat(.a)),
                     B = .conv_ess(.a$min_ess_bulk), T = .conv_ess(.a$min_ess_tail),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  les_grid_table(body,
                 header = .les_widths(c("Fit", "$\\widehat{R}$", "Bulk", "Tail"),
                                      pdf = c(.58, .10, .10, .10)),
                 align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"),
                 spanners = list(list(label = "ESS", cols = 3:4)),
                 group = .les_group(.a$prop))
} else {
  knitr::asis_output("*Convergence diagnostics will appear here once the models are fitted.*")
}
```

# Group displays by session {#apx-group-sessions}

The main-text group displays pool each property's sessions. This appendix resolves them by
session, so that the development the models estimate can be inspected in each group. Like
the pooled displays, they are descriptive and were not used to select any analysis.
@fig-erp-difference-sessions gives the difference waves at the midline posterior cluster and
@fig-erp-topography-sessions the late-window maps. The observed judgement accuracies behind
@fig-sdt-by-language are given in @fig-accuracy-by-language.

```{r}
#| label: fig-erp-difference-sessions
#| fig-cap: "Difference Waves (Ungrammatical Minus Grammatical) at the Midline Posterior Cluster by Session, Miniature Language and Property"
#| apa-note: "Each line is the participant-paired difference between ungrammatical and grammatical baseline-corrected waveforms at the midline posterior cluster at one session, averaged over participants, for the Mini-Norwegian (blue) and Mini-English (vermilion) groups. Ribbons are pointwise 95% normal intervals from the participant-level standard error. Cells are blank at sessions before a property was introduced, since differential object marking entered the design at Session 3 and verb--object number agreement at Session 4. Sessions 2 to 4 are a week apart. Session 6 is the retention test, about four months after Session 4 without exposure, and draws on fewer participants (see the participant flow figure). Polarity, window bars and the next-word triangle are as in the pooled difference-wave figure in the Results."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: !expr if (group_figures_ready) 6.3 else 1
if (!is.null(dwv)) {
  ds <- dwv[dwv$brain_region == "midline posterior" & dwv$session != "pooled", ]
  # Rows in time order and columns in design order, as factors with their full level
  # sets, so that les_blank_cells() can find the cells the design leaves empty.
  ds$Session <- factor(paste("Session", ds$session), levels = paste("Session", LES_ERP_SESSIONS))
  ds$Property <- les_property_factor(ds$grammatical_property)
  ds$Language <- factor(ds$mini_language, levels = .lang_levels)
  frE <- les_erp_frame(min(ds$mean_difference - 1.96 * ds$se_difference),
                       max(ds$mean_difference + 1.96 * ds$se_difference), seq(-4, 4, 2))
  # The legend goes in the top-right cell, which the staircase of the exposure schedule
  # leaves empty (the last property at the first session); below the plot if it is not.
  .tr_empty <- !any(ds$Session == levels(ds$Session)[1] &
                    ds$Property == levels(ds$Property)[nlevels(ds$Property)])
  # The blanking rectangles also get a white outline: a grid or reference line that
  # ends on the edge of an absent cell otherwise survives there as a hairline.
  .blank <- les_blank_cells(ds, "Session", "Property")
  .blank$aes_params[c("colour", "linewidth")] <- list("white", 1)
  ggplot(ds, aes(time, mean_difference, colour = Language, fill = Language)) +
    les_erp_layers(frE, .next_word_ms) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = mean_difference - 1.96 * se_difference,
                    ymax = mean_difference + 1.96 * se_difference),
                alpha = 0.18, colour = NA) +
    geom_line(linewidth = LES_LWD_TRACE) +
    facet_grid(Session ~ Property, labeller = labeller(Property = les_wrap(20))) +
    les_scale_language() +
    labs(x = "Time from critical-word onset (ms)",
         y = "Ungrammatical − grammatical (µV)") +
    les_theme() + theme(strip.text.x = element_text(vjust = 0)) +
    (if (.tr_empty)
       theme(legend.position = "inside", legend.position.inside = c(1, 1),
             legend.justification.inside = c(1, 1), legend.direction = "vertical")
     else theme(legend.position = "bottom")) +
    # Last layer: paints the absent cells white over grid, reference lines and window bars.
    .blank
} else {
  les_placeholder("Session-resolved difference waves pending the updated extraction")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-erp-topography-sessions
#| fig-cap: "Scalp Topography of the Grammaticality Effect by Property, Session and Miniature Language, 400--900 ms"
#| apa-note: "Maps show the participant-paired ungrammatical-minus-grammatical mean amplitude in the 400--900 ms window at each session, baseline-corrected within participant and averaged over participants. Each block is one property, with sessions in columns and the Mini-Norwegian and Mini-English groups in rows. Only the sessions at which a property was tested are shown: gender agreement from Session 2, differential object marking from Session 3, and verb--object number agreement at Sessions 4 and 6. Sessions 2 to 4 are a week apart. Session 6 is the retention test, about four months after Session 4 without exposure, and draws on fewer participants (see the participant flow figure). Surface estimation, montage, symbols, polarity and the colour scale are those of the scalp-topography figure in the Results, so colours can be compared directly between the two figures."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: !expr if (group_figures_ready) 2.1 else 1
# The surfaces (ts), the colour limit and the block helper come from the scalp-topography
# chunk in the Results, so the two figures share one estimation, one map size and one
# colour scale.
if (!is.null(ts) && !is.null(ts$surf)) {
  for (nm in c("surf", "sensors")) {
    ts[[nm]]$Property <- les_property_factor(ts[[nm]]$grammatical_property)
    ts[[nm]]$Group    <- factor(ts[[nm]]$mini_language, levels = LES_LANG_LEVELS)
  }
  ts$sensors <- ts$sensors[!duplicated(ts$sensors[c("Property", "session", "Group", "electrode")]), ]
  .ts_props <- levels(droplevels(ts$surf$Property))
  .topo_e2 <- lapply(seq_along(.ts_props), function(i) {
    sub <- .topo_subset(ts, function(d) d$Property == .ts_props[i])
    # Columns are only the sessions at which the property was tested, so no block
    # carries an empty cell.
    lv <- intersect(LES_ERP_SESSIONS, unique(sub$surf$session))
    for (nm in c("surf", "sensors"))
      sub[[nm]]$Session <- factor(paste("Session", sub[[nm]]$session), levels = paste("Session", lv))
    # A two-map block is too narrow for the longest property name on one line; the
    # one-line titles are bottom-aligned with it (vjust = 0 in .topo_block()).
    title <- if (length(lv) <= 2) paste(strwrap(.ts_props[i], 20), collapse = "\n") else .ts_props[i]
    .topo_block(sub, "Group", "Session", .topo_lim, title = title, show_rows = i == 1) +
      theme(plot.margin = margin(1, 4, 1, 4))
  })
  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(patchwork))
  patchwork::wrap_plots(.topo_e2, nrow = 1, guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
} else {
  les_placeholder("Session-resolved topographies pending the updated extraction")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-accuracy-by-language
#| fig-cap: "Observed Judgement Accuracy by Sentence Type, Miniature Language, Property and Session"
#| apa-note: "Points are group means of participant-level proportion correct on grammatical sentences (upper row) and on ungrammatical sentences (lower row), and every participant receives equal weight. Vertical lines are 95% *t* intervals over participants, and the horizontal line marks chance (.50). Each property is plotted from the session at which it entered the design. Accuracy on the two sentence types moves in opposite directions when a group's criterion shifts, which is why the Results analyse sensitivity and criterion and not accuracy on either sentence type. Sessions are equally spaced, as in the models, although Sessions 2 to 4 are a week apart and Session 6 follows about four months without exposure."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: !expr if (group_figures_ready && file.exists(paper1_results("_accuracy_by_language.csv"))) 4.8 else 1
acc_group <- .read_csv_if(paper1_results("_accuracy_by_language.csv"))
if (group_figures_ready && !is.null(acc_group)) {
  # The encoding of the sensitivity and criterion figure: sentence type is a row (never a
  # linetype or an open symbol), and language takes colour plus shape.
  acc_group <- les_judgement_frame(acc_group)
  stopifnot(!anyNA(acc_group$Property))
  acc_group$Sentence <- factor(acc_group$grammaticality, levels = c("Grammatical", "Ungrammatical"),
                               labels = c("Grammatical sentences\n(proportion correct)",
                                          "Ungrammatical sentences\n(proportion correct)"))
  ggplot(acc_group, aes(Session, mean_accuracy, colour = Language, shape = Language,
                        group = Language)) +
    les_ref_h(0.5) +
    les_judgement_layers() +
    facet_grid(Sentence ~ Property, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x", switch = "y",
               labeller = labeller(Property = les_wrap(18))) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25), labels = les_lab_prop) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    les_scale_language() + les_scale_language_shape() +
    labs(x = "Session") +
    les_judgement_theme() + les_row_title_theme() +
    theme(strip.text.x = element_text(vjust = 0))   # labels on one baseline, as in Figure 11
} else {
  les_placeholder("Observed accuracy pending the updated extraction")
}
```
